key_figures.research_focus: Works on forced migration, humanitarianism, and international humanitarian law, with a focus on South Asia, gender, and conflict-related displacement. Her research examines protection, peacekeeping, and the politics of humanitarian intervention.

key_figures.name: Sara E. Davies
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Researches forced migration, global health governance, and humanitarian responses, particularly in the Asia-Pacific. Her work addresses refugee protection, human rights, and the politics of humanitarianism.

key_figures.name: Anthea Roberts
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Specialises in international law, including international humanitarian law and the laws of armed conflict. Her research examines how international legal norms operate across different geopolitical and institutional contexts.

title: ANU Fenner School of Environment and Society HDR Scholarship
summary: The Fenner School HDR Scholarship supports PhD research on environment-society interactions, including disaster management, climate-related migration, and global health. It generally provides a stipend and tuition fee coverage.

key_figures.name: Helen James
key_figures.title: Emeritus Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on disaster risk reduction, humanitarian action, and governance in Southeast Asia, with a focus on the politics of disaster management and forced migration.

key_figures.name: Kamalini Lokuge
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Global health researcher focusing on health in humanitarian crises, forced migration, and disease control in conflict-affected and displaced populations.

key_figures.name: Sara E. Davies
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on global health governance, health security, and the politics of pandemic response, including the health dimensions of migration and displacement.

title: Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP) Scholarship at Monash
summary: The Australian Government Research Training Program Scholarship, administered at Monash University, provides tuition fee offsets and stipends to both domestic and international higher degree by research candidates. It supports doctoral research across all fields, including global health and humanitarian studies.

key_figures.name: Bebe Loff
key_figures.title: Professor, Director of the Michael Kirby Centre for Public Health and Human Rights
key_figures.research_focus: Works at the intersection of public health, human rights, and law, with a focus on the health of marginalized populations including refugees and asylum seekers.

key_figures.name: Helen Forbes-Mewett
key_figures.title: Associate Professor, Sociology
key_figures.research_focus: Researches migration, international students, and social inclusion, with attention to the vulnerabilities and wellbeing of displaced and mobile populations.

key_figures.name: Alex Broom
key_figures.title: Professor of Sociology, Director of the Sydney Centre for Healthy Societies
key_figures.research_focus: Examines global health, humanitarianism, and the social dimensions of health crises, including work on refugee health and humanitarian responses.

title: Monash-Warwick Alliance PhD Scholarship
summary: The Monash-Warwick Alliance supports joint PhD scholarships between Monash University and the University of Warwick, enabling doctoral research with international supervision. Projects can address themes relevant to global health, humanitarian studies, and forced migration.

key_figures.name: Bebe Loff
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Global health and human rights, with work on health equity, humanitarianism, and the health of marginalized populations including refugees and displaced people.

key_figures.name: Michael G. Findley
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Political science and humanitarian studies, focusing on forced migration, refugee policy, conflict-affected populations, and global health interventions in fragile settings.

key_figures.name: Alexandra Devine
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Global health and humanitarian practice, with research on forced migration, refugee health, and health systems in humanitarian emergencies.

title: University of Otago Health Sciences PhD Scholarship
summary: The Division of Health Sciences at Otago offers doctoral scholarships supporting PhD research in health-related fields, including global and public health topics relevant to conflict and disaster contexts. Awards generally cover fees and provide a stipend.

key_figures.name: Philip Hill
key_figures.title: Professor of International Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global health with a focus on infectious disease epidemiology, tuberculosis, and health in low-resource and conflict-affected settings. Leads international health research at the University of Otago's Centre for International Health.

key_figures.name: Michael Baker
key_figures.title: Professor of Public Health
key_figures.research_focus: Public health, epidemiology, and infectious disease control, including pandemic preparedness and global health security. Widely cited for work on COVID-19 and public health policy.

key_figures.name: Jacqueline Cumming
key_figures.title: Professor of Health Policy
key_figures.research_focus: Health policy and health systems research, including global health governance and equity in health service delivery. Former director of the Health Services Research Centre.

title: Victoria University of Wellington Postgraduate Research Scholarship
summary: Victoria University of Wellington offers a range of postgraduate research scholarships that may provide partial or full support for PhD candidates. These awards are often faculty- or project-specific and can be relevant to health, social science, and humanitarian research topics.

title: New Zealand Government Scholarship (NZ Scholarship) - Doctoral
summary: New Zealand Government Scholarships fund postgraduate and doctoral study at New Zealand universities, including the University of Auckland, for students from developing countries, with priority given to fields such as health, development and disaster risk reduction. They cover tuition, living costs and travel.

key_figures.name: Alistair Woodward
key_figures.title: Professor of Epidemiology and Biostatistics
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on the health impacts of climate change, environmental epidemiology, and global health policy. He has contributed to international assessments on climate change and health, including work with the IPCC and WHO.

key_figures.name: David Johnston
key_figures.title: Professor of Disaster Management
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on disaster risk reduction, emergency management, and community resilience, particularly in the context of volcanic hazards and natural disasters. He leads the Joint Centre for Disaster Research.

key_figures.name: Sione Vaka
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer in Nursing
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on Pacific health, mental health, and culturally responsive approaches to global health and humanitarian contexts. He has worked on health equity and community-based interventions in Pacific communities.

title: University of Auckland Faculty of Arts Doctoral Scholarship
summary: Faculty of Arts doctoral scholarships at the University of Auckland support PhD research in humanities and social sciences, including development studies, migration, peace and conflict studies. They typically cover fees and provide a stipend for the duration of study.

key_figures.name: Jay Marlowe
key_figures.title: Professor of Social Work and Co-Director, Centre for Asia Pacific Refugee Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Research on forced migration, refugee settlement and belonging, and community-based responses to displacement. He has led major studies on refugee resettlement in New Zealand and the Asia-Pacific region.

key_figures.name: Anna Hood
key_figures.title: Associate Professor, Faculty of Law
key_figures.research_focus: Research on international humanitarian law, international criminal law, and the regulation of armed conflict. Her work examines humanitarian protection and legal accountability in conflict settings.

key_figures.name: Carolyn Morris
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer, Faculty of Law
key_figures.research_focus: Research on international human rights law, refugee law, and humanitarian studies, with attention to the legal protection of forced migrants and asylum seekers.

title: UC Connect Doctoral Scholarship
summary: The UC Connect Doctoral Scholarship is a fully-funded doctoral award at the University of Canterbury that supports research aligned with university priority areas, which can include disaster resilience, humanitarian studies, and global health. It provides tuition fees and a stipend for the duration of the PhD.

key_figures.name: David Johnston
key_figures.title: Professor of Disaster Management
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on disaster risk reduction, emergency management, and community resilience, with extensive work on volcanic hazards and public health impacts of disasters.

key_figures.name: Thomas Wilson
key_figures.title: Professor of Disaster Risk and Resilience
key_figures.research_focus: Researches disaster risk and resilience, volcanic hazard and risk assessment, and the intersection of disaster management with public health and humanitarian response.

key_figures.name: Ann Brower
key_figures.title: Professor of Environmental Policy and Planning
key_figures.research_focus: Examines disaster governance, humanitarian policy, and the social dimensions of disaster management, including global health implications of environmental change.

title: Commonwealth Scholarship (New Zealand)
summary: The Commonwealth Scholarship scheme enables students from Commonwealth countries to undertake PhD study at the University of Canterbury, with funding covering tuition, stipend, and travel. It is applicable to research in global health, humanitarian studies, disaster management, and forced migration.

key_figures.name: David Johnston
key_figures.title: Professor of Disaster Management
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on disaster risk reduction, emergency management, and community resilience, with extensive work on volcanic hazards and integrated disaster planning in New Zealand and internationally.

key_figures.name: Thomas Wilson
key_figures.title: Professor of Disaster Risk and Resilience
key_figures.research_focus: Researches disaster risk and resilience, volcanic hazard and risk assessment, and the intersection of science with emergency management and humanitarian response.

key_figures.name: Ann Brower
key_figures.title: Professor of Environmental Politics and Governance
key_figures.research_focus: Examines environmental governance, disaster recovery policy, and the political dimensions of humanitarian and global health crises, particularly in post-disaster contexts.

title: Marsden Fund Doctoral Scholarship
summary: The Marsden Fund, administered by the Royal Society Te Apārangi, supports excellent research in New Zealand, and doctoral scholarships are often associated with Marsden-funded projects at the University of Canterbury. These can cover fields such as disaster management, global health, and humanitarian studies, providing fees and stipend.

title: Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) North West Social Science Doctoral Training Partnership (NWSSDTP) Studentship
summary: The ESRC North West Social Science Doctoral Training Partnership funds PhD studentships at the University of Manchester and other North West institutions. Studentships cover fees and a stipend and support social science research including migration, humanitarian studies, and global health topics.

key_figures.name: Jenny Phillimore
key_figures.title: Professor of Migration and Superdiversity
key_figures.research_focus: Research on migration, refugee integration, and the experiences of forced migrants, with a focus on how local services and policies shape settlement outcomes.

key_figures.name: Rebecca Tipton
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer in Translation and Interpreting Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Works on language, translation, and interpreting in humanitarian and forced migration contexts, including communication with refugees and asylum seekers.

key_figures.name: Mukesh Kapila
key_figures.title: Professor in Practice, Global Health and Humanitarian Affairs
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on global health, humanitarian crises, conflict, and forced displacement, drawing on extensive international policy and humanitarian practice experience.

title: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships (for low and middle income countries) - University of Manchester
summary: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships are funded by the UK government and can be hosted at the University of Manchester, supporting doctoral candidates from low and middle income countries. They cover tuition fees, stipend, airfare, and other allowances, and can support research in global health, humanitarian studies, and forced migration.

key_figures.name: Mukesh Kapila
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Humanitarian Affairs
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health policy, humanitarian crises, conflict and atrocity prevention, with extensive experience in UN and international humanitarian operations.

key_figures.name: Jenny Peterson
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer in Human Geography
key_figures.research_focus: Researches forced migration, refugee settlement, humanitarian governance, and the politics of displacement and asylum.

key_figures.name: Tanja Müller
key_figures.title: Professor of Political Sociology
key_figures.research_focus: Examines forced migration, refugee livelihoods, humanitarianism, and African politics, with a focus on displacement and social transformation.

title: King's College London PGR Studentship (King's Doctoral Studentship)
summary: King's College London offers competitive doctoral studentships covering tuition fees and a stipend for outstanding PhD candidates across its faculties, including the Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine and the School of Global Affairs. These studentships support research in areas such as global health, conflict and health, and humanitarian studies.

key_figures.name: Richard Sullivan
key_figures.title: Professor of Cancer and Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on global health systems, cancer care in low- and middle-income countries, and health in conflict-affected and humanitarian settings. Directs the Institute of Cancer Policy and works on health system strengthening in fragile states.

key_figures.name: Preeti Patel
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the intersection of health, conflict, and humanitarian action, including health system resilience in conflict-affected states and the politics of humanitarian health assistance. Leads the Conflict and Health Research Group.

key_figures.name: Gemma Bowsher
key_figures.title: Senior Research Fellow in Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Examines global health security, humanitarian response, and the health impacts of conflict and complex emergencies. Works on health system governance and emergency preparedness in fragile settings.

title: King's College London – London Interdisciplinary Social Science Doctoral Training Partnership (LISS DTP) Studentship (ESRC)
summary: The ESRC-funded LISS DTP provides fully-funded PhD studentships hosted at King's College London and other London institutions, covering fees and a stipend. It supports social science research including forced migration, humanitarian studies, and related interdisciplinary fields.

key_figures.name: Dr. Nicola Perugini
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer in International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international humanitarian law, the politics of human rights, and the legal and spatial dimensions of forced displacement and occupation, with a focus on Israel/Palestine and the Mediterranean.

key_figures.name: Professor Jenny Edkins
key_figures.title: Professor of International Politics
key_figures.research_focus: Researches forced displacement, humanitarianism, and the politics of memory and trauma, including critical analyses of refugee camps, humanitarian intervention, and state responses to displacement.

key_figures.name: Dr. Ruben Andersson
key_figures.title: Associate Professor in Anthropology
key_figures.research_focus: Anthropologist of migration and borders whose work examines forced migration, humanitarian border regimes, and the unintended consequences of migration control across West Africa and the Mediterranean.

title: King's College London – Wellcome Trust Doctoral Studentship
summary: Wellcome Trust funding supports doctoral research at King's College London in biomedical and health-related fields, including global and public health. These studentships typically cover full tuition and a stipend for the duration of the PhD.

key_figures.name: Richard Sullivan
key_figures.title: Professor of Cancer and Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on global health systems, health in conflict-affected settings, and the interface between health, security, and humanitarian response. Directs the Institute of Cancer Policy and has published extensively on health in conflict and post-conflict environments.

key_figures.name: Preeti Patel
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the intersection of global health, conflict, and security, with a focus on health systems in fragile and conflict-affected states, humanitarian access, and the politics of health emergencies.

key_figures.name: Gemma Bowsher
key_figures.title: Research Fellow in Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Examines the intersections of global health, conflict, and security, including health system resilience in conflict zones and the securitisation of health. Works within the Conflict and Health Research Group at King's College London.

title: King's College London – Chevening Scholarship (PhD eligible)
summary: Chevening is the UK government's international scholarship programme, and King's College London is a host institution. It funds master's degrees primarily, though some doctoral study may be supported; it covers tuition, living costs, and travel for outstanding international students.

key_figures.name: Richard Sullivan
key_figures.title: Professor of Cancer and Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on global health systems, humanitarian health, and the delivery of health services in conflict-affected and low-resource settings. His work spans cancer care in humanitarian crises and health system strengthening.

key_figures.name: Preeti Patel
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the intersections of conflict, forced migration, and health, including humanitarian response, health systems in fragile states, and the health of displaced populations.

key_figures.name: Simon Wessely
key_figures.title: Professor of Psychological Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Investigates the mental health consequences of conflict, forced migration, and humanitarian emergencies, with a focus on military and refugee populations.

title: King's College London – Commonwealth Scholarship (PhD)
summary: Commonwealth Scholarships fund PhD study at UK universities including King's College London for students from low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries. They cover tuition fees, airfare, and a living allowance, and support research in development-related fields such as global health and humanitarian studies.

key_figures.name: Richard Sullivan
key_figures.title: Professor of Cancer and Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on global health systems, health in conflict and humanitarian settings, and the interface between health, security, and development. His work addresses cancer care in low- and middle-income countries and health system strengthening in fragile states.

key_figures.name: Preeti Patel
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the intersections of global health, conflict, and forced migration, including health system resilience in conflict-affected states and humanitarian responses to displacement. She leads work on health in fragile and conflict-affected settings at King's College London.

key_figures.name: Jenny Phillimore
key_figures.title: Professor of Migration and Superdiversity
key_figures.research_focus: Conducts research on forced migration, refugee integration, and the governance of migration, with a focus on the experiences of refugees and asylum seekers in the UK and Europe. Her work spans humanitarian studies and migration policy.

title: King's College London – AHRC London Arts and Humanities Partnership (LAHP) Studentship
summary: The AHRC-funded LAHP provides fully-funded doctoral studentships at King's College London and other London institutions in arts and humanities disciplines. It can support research in international humanitarian law, forced migration, and humanitarian studies within relevant departments.

key_figures.name: Dr. Sarah Singer
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer in Refugee Law
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on forced migration, refugee law, and the legal frameworks governing asylum and displacement. She examines how international humanitarian law and human rights law intersect with refugee protection.

key_figures.name: Professor Guglielmo Verdirame
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the law of international organizations, with particular attention to humanitarian action and forced displacement. His research addresses legal accountability in armed conflict and refugee protection.

key_figures.name: Dr. Leonie Ansems de Vries
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer in International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Researches forced migration, humanitarianism, and the politics of displacement, with a focus on refugee governance and humanitarian border practices. Her work critically examines humanitarian studies and migration management.

title: LSE Department of Health Policy PhD Studentship
summary: The Department of Health Policy at LSE offers funded doctoral studentships for research in health policy and global health. Funding generally includes tuition fees and a stipend for eligible PhD candidates.

key_figures.name: Tim Allen
key_figures.title: Professor in Development Anthropology
key_figures.research_focus: Research on conflict, humanitarianism, and health in war-affected regions, including northern Uganda and South Sudan. Examines the intersections of violence, displacement, and public health interventions.

key_figures.name: Clare Wenham
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of Global Health Policy
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health governance, pandemic preparedness, and health security, with attention to fragile and conflict-affected settings. Has published on the politics of global health emergencies and health system resilience.

key_figures.name: Bayard Roberts
key_figures.title: Professor of Health Systems and Policy
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on health systems and mental health in conflict-affected populations, including studies on Syria, Ukraine, and other humanitarian settings. Focuses on strengthening health systems in fragile states.

title: LSE Middle East Centre PhD Scholarship
summary: The LSE Middle East Centre offers PhD scholarships for research related to the Middle East, including topics such as conflict, displacement, and humanitarian issues. Awards typically cover fees and a stipend.

key_figures.name: Michael Bruter
key_figures.title: Professor of Political Science and European Politics
key_figures.research_focus: Research on political behaviour, identity, and the effects of conflict and displacement on political attitudes and participation.

key_figures.name: Eiko Thielemann
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of Political Science and Public Policy
key_figures.research_focus: Works on forced migration, asylum and refugee policy, and European and international responses to displacement and humanitarian crises.

key_figures.name: Bayard Roberts
key_figures.title: Professor of Health Systems and Policy
key_figures.research_focus: Research on health in conflict-affected and humanitarian settings, including forced migration, mental health, and health system responses.

title: Wellcome Trust Doctoral Studentship in Global Health
summary: Wellcome Trust funds doctoral studentships in global health research, often hosted at UK universities and advertised via FindAPhD. These studentships typically cover tuition, stipend, and research costs for projects related to global health, humanitarian crises, and health in conflict settings.

title: ESRC Doctoral Studentship in Forced Migration and Humanitarian Studies
summary: Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) doctoral studentships fund PhD research across social sciences, including forced migration, humanitarian studies, and disaster management. These are hosted at UK universities and frequently listed on FindAPhD, covering fees and a stipend.

title: Commonwealth PhD Scholarship
summary: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships fund doctoral study at UK universities for candidates from low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries. Relevant fields include global health, humanitarian studies, and forced migration, with full tuition and stipend support.

title: Chevening Scholarship
summary: Chevening Scholarships are UK government-funded awards supporting outstanding scholars from around the world to pursue postgraduate study in the UK, including PhDs in fields such as international humanitarian law and global health. They cover tuition, living costs, and travel.

title: DAAD Research Grant for Doctoral Candidates
summary: DAAD Research Grants support international doctoral candidates conducting research in Germany, including in global health, humanitarian studies, and disaster management. The grant provides monthly stipend, travel allowance, and health insurance.

title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship
summary: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships fund doctoral research at Swiss universities for international scholars, including fields such as global health, humanitarian studies, and international humanitarian law. Awards cover monthly stipend, tuition, and insurance.

title: Eiffel Excellence Scholarship Program (Doctoral Track)
summary: The Eiffel Excellence Scholarship Program, managed by Campus France, funds international PhD students to pursue doctoral studies in France. It provides a monthly stipend, travel costs, health insurance, and cultural activities for up to 12 months (renewable for a second year). Applicants must be nominated by a French host institution.

title: Make Our Planet Great Again (MOPGA) Doctoral Program
summary: The MOPGA program, coordinated by Campus France, supports international doctoral students whose research addresses climate change and related challenges, including disaster risk and environmental migration. It offers a monthly living allowance, relocation support, and health coverage for up to 12 months, renewable.

title: Campus France Doctoral Scholarships for Developing Countries
summary: Campus France administers various doctoral scholarship schemes for students from developing countries, often in partnership with French embassies and research institutions. These cover tuition, monthly stipend, travel, and insurance for PhD research in France, including topics in global health and humanitarian studies.

title: French Government Scholarship (BGF) - Doctoral Studies
summary: The French Government Scholarship (BGF), managed through Campus France and French embassies, supports international PhD candidates in priority research areas. It typically includes a monthly stipend, travel, and health insurance for the duration of doctoral studies in France.

title: EDUFI Doctoral Studies Grant for International Students
summary: EDUFI offers grants to international doctoral students who are pursuing a PhD at a Finnish university and who do not receive other Finnish government funding. The grant contributes to living costs and is intended for doctoral candidates conducting research in fields such as global health, humanitarian studies, and international humanitarian law.

title: PhD Scholarship in Global Health (University of Copenhagen)
summary: The University of Copenhagen's Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences regularly advertises fully-funded PhD scholarships in global health and related areas. These positions typically cover salary, tuition, and research costs for a three-year doctoral programme. Specific projects vary by call and supervisor.

key_figures.name: Flemming Konradsen
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global health with emphasis on environmental health, water and sanitation, and health systems in low-income settings. Leads research on disease prevention and health promotion in resource-constrained populations.

key_figures.name: Ib Christian Bygbjerg
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global health and infectious diseases, including malaria, diabetes in low-income countries, and maternal-child health. Works on health systems strengthening and disease prevention in developing regions.

key_figures.name: Ditte Linde
key_figures.title: Associate Professor, Public Health
key_figures.research_focus: Public health research focusing on health promotion, prevention, and health systems. Investigates social determinants of health and interventions to improve population health outcomes.

title: PhD Fellowship in Public Health and Epidemiology
summary: The Department of Public Health at the University of Copenhagen offers PhD fellowships in epidemiology, global health, and health in humanitarian settings. Fellowships are fully funded for three years and include salary and travel/research expenses. Positions are advertised on an ongoing basis.

key_figures.name: Flemming Konradsen
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global health with focus on environmental health, injury prevention, and health in low-income settings. Leads research on water, sanitation, and health in humanitarian and development contexts.

key_figures.name: Peter Aaby
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Epidemiology and global health, particularly non-specific effects of vaccines and child health in low-income countries. Long-standing research in Guinea-Bissau on infectious disease epidemiology.

key_figures.name: Jens Seeberg
key_figures.title: Professor, Anthropology and Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Medical anthropology and global health, with research on health systems, conflict-affected populations, and mental health in humanitarian settings.

title: Danish Council for Independent Research (DFF) PhD Scholarship
summary: The Danish Council for Independent Research funds PhD scholarships hosted at Danish universities including the University of Copenhagen. These grants support independent research projects across health, social sciences, and humanities, including global health and humanitarian topics. Funding covers salary and research costs for a three-year PhD.

key_figures.name: Flemming Konradsen
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global health with focus on environmental health, water and sanitation, and health in low-income settings. Leads research on disease prevention and health promotion in resource-poor communities.

key_figures.name: Peter Vedsted
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Health systems research, cancer diagnostics, and primary care in global health contexts. Works on improving access to healthcare and reducing inequalities in health outcomes.

key_figures.name: Morten Sodemann
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global health and humanitarian medicine, with emphasis on migrant health, infectious diseases, and health equity. Involved in research on vulnerable populations and health interventions in low-resource settings.

title: Danish Institute for International Studies (DIIS) PhD Scholarship
summary: DIIS, in collaboration with the University of Copenhagen, occasionally offers PhD scholarships focused on humanitarian studies, forced migration, and conflict. These are fully-funded positions for three years, often linked to specific research projects. Candidates should monitor DIIS and university job portals for calls.

key_figures.name: Finn Stepputat
key_figures.title: Senior Researcher, Danish Institute for International Studies; formerly affiliated with University of Copenhagen
key_figures.research_focus: Research on forced migration, humanitarianism, sovereignty, and conflict, with a focus on displacement and governance in fragile states.

key_figures.name: Anja Kublitz
key_figures.title: Associate Professor, Department of Anthropology, University of Copenhagen
key_figures.research_focus: Research on forced migration, refugee families, humanitarianism, and the aftermath of conflict, particularly among Palestinian refugees.

key_figures.name: Zachary Whyte
key_figures.title: Associate Professor, Department of Sociology, University of Copenhagen
key_figures.research_focus: Research on refugee reception, asylum, humanitarian governance, and forced migration in Denmark and Europe.

title: University of Copenhagen PhD Scholarship in Law (International Humanitarian Law)
summary: The Faculty of Law at the University of Copenhagen offers fully-funded PhD scholarships, including in international humanitarian law and human rights. These are typically three-year positions with salary and research support. Calls are announced on the faculty's PhD page.

key_figures.name: Mikael Rask Madsen
key_figures.title: Professor, PhD
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on international law, human rights, and the sociology of international courts and legal institutions. He has written extensively on the European Court of Human Rights and the transformation of international law.

key_figures.name: Jens Elo Rytter
key_figures.title: Professor, PhD
key_figures.research_focus: Research centers on constitutional law, human rights law, and international human rights conventions, particularly their implementation in Danish and European legal systems.

key_figures.name: Martin Mennecke
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on international humanitarian law, international criminal law, and human rights, with particular attention to the responsibility to protect and atrocity prevention.

title: Copenhagen School of Global Health PhD Scholarship
summary: The Copenhagen School of Global Health at the University of Copenhagen coordinates PhD training and research in global health, including disaster management and health in conflict. Fully-funded PhD positions are advertised through the school and its partner institutions. Funding covers salary and research costs.

key_figures.name: Peter Aaby
key_figures.title: Professor Emeritus
key_figures.research_focus: Conducts research on global health, particularly on the non-specific effects of vaccines and child survival in low-income countries, with extensive fieldwork in Guinea-Bissau.

key_figures.name: Christine Stabell Benn
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Researches global health and the beneficial non-specific effects of vaccines on overall health and survival, with a focus on low-income settings and health interventions.

key_figures.name: Flemming Konradsen
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health, disaster management, and environmental health, including research on injury prevention, water and sanitation, and health in humanitarian crises.

title: Croatian Government Scholarship for Foreign Students (Bilateral Programme)
summary: The Ministry of Science and Education of Croatia offers bilateral scholarships to foreign students and researchers, including doctoral-level study, based on intergovernmental agreements. Funding typically covers tuition, monthly stipend, accommodation, and health insurance for the duration of study.

title: Croatian Government Scholarship for Croatian Diaspora (Doctoral Studies)
summary: The Central State Office for Croats Abroad and the Ministry of Science and Education provide scholarships supporting members of the Croatian diaspora pursuing doctoral studies in Croatia. Support may include tuition assistance and stipends, subject to annual calls.

title: CEEPUS Doctoral Mobility Scholarship (Central European Exchange Programme for University Studies)
summary: CEEPUS is a regional mobility programme in which Croatia participates, offering scholarships for doctoral students to study and research at Croatian universities within approved networks. It provides monthly stipends, travel support, and tuition waivers for mobility periods.

title: PhD Scholarship in International Relations/Political Science (Graduate Institute Geneva)
summary: The Graduate Institute offers competitive fully-funded PhD scholarships to admitted doctoral students in its International Relations/Political Science programme, covering tuition and providing a living stipend. Research at the Institute frequently addresses humanitarian action, conflict, migration, and global governance.

key_figures.name: Mohammad-Mahmoud Ould Mohamedou
key_figures.title: Professor of International History and Politics
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international relations, political violence, state-building, and the history of humanitarianism and intervention, with a focus on the Middle East and Africa.

key_figures.name: Davide Rodogno
key_figures.title: Professor of International History and Politics
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the history of humanitarianism, humanitarian intervention, international organizations, and transnational governance in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

key_figures.name: Stephanie Hofmann
key_figures.title: Professor of International Relations and Political Science
key_figures.research_focus: Studies international security, international organizations, peacekeeping, and the politics of multilateral intervention, including humanitarian dimensions of security governance.

title: PhD Scholarship in International Law (Graduate Institute Geneva)
summary: Doctoral scholarships are available for the PhD in International Law at the Graduate Institute, supporting research including international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the law of armed conflict. Funding typically covers tuition and living costs for the duration of the programme.

key_figures.name: Andrew Clapham
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the regulation of armed conflict, including the law of war and the role of non-state actors.

key_figures.name: Paola Gaeta
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international criminal law, international humanitarian law, and human rights, with emphasis on accountability for serious international crimes.

key_figures.name: Nico Krisch
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Examines international law and human rights, including the politics of international legal authority and the changing structures of global governance.

title: PhD Scholarship in Development Studies (Graduate Institute Geneva)
summary: The Graduate Institute's PhD in Development Studies offers funded doctoral positions for research on development, humanitarianism, health, and migration. Scholarships generally include tuition waivers and a monthly stipend.

title: Qatar Research Leadership Program (QRLP) Doctoral Scholarship
summary: The Qatar Research Leadership Program (QRLP) is a Qatar Foundation initiative that funds outstanding students to pursue PhD studies at leading international universities in fields aligned with Qatar's research priorities, including health and social sciences. It provides full tuition, stipend, and research support, with scholars expected to contribute to Qatar's research ecosystem upon completion.

title: Qatar University Graduate Scholarship (PhD)
summary: Qatar University offers fully-funded graduate scholarships for PhD candidates, including tuition waiver, monthly stipend, and housing. While Qatar University is a national institution, Qatar Foundation-affiliated students and researchers frequently access these awards for health and social science research relevant to humanitarian and migration studies.

title: Fogarty Global Health Fellowship (Global Health Fellows and Scholars Program)
summary: The Fogarty Global Health Fellows and Scholars Program supports mentored clinical research training for pre- and postdoctoral fellows, including doctoral-level trainees, at partner sites in low- and middle-income countries. It provides stipend, travel, and research support for a year of global health research training. It is administered through NIH Fogarty International Center and its consortium partners.

title: Fogarty HIV Research Training Program (D43)
summary: The Fogarty HIV Research Training Program funds institutional research training grants that support doctoral and postdoctoral trainees in HIV-related research, often through partnerships between U.S. and low- and middle-income country institutions. Trainees may receive stipends, tuition, and research support as part of these D43 training programs. It is a flagship Fogarty mechanism for building global HIV research capacity.

title: Fogarty Emerging Global Leader Award (K43)
summary: The Fogarty Emerging Global Leader Award provides mentored research career development support to early-career scientists from low- and middle-income countries. While aimed at postdoctoral and early faculty researchers, it funds protected research time and training that can include doctoral-level global health research capacity building. It is a Fogarty K43 career development award.

title: Fogarty Global Infectious Disease Research Training Program (D43)
summary: The Fogarty Global Infectious Disease Research Training Program funds institutional training grants that support doctoral and postdoctoral trainees in infectious disease research at LMIC institutions. Trainees receive stipends, tuition support, and mentored research training. It is one of Fogarty's core D43 research training mechanisms.

title: Fogarty Mobile Health (mHealth) Research Training Program
summary: The Fogarty Mobile Health Research Training Program supports training of doctoral and postdoctoral researchers in mobile health technologies for global health settings. It funds institutional training grants that provide stipends, tuition, and research support to trainees. It is part of Fogarty's efforts to build capacity in digital health research.

title: Aga Khan University Institute for Human Development PhD Research
summary: The Aga Khan University Institute for Human Development conducts research and doctoral training related to human development, early childhood, and social determinants of health, with relevance to vulnerable and displaced populations. Doctoral candidates may pursue funded research within its programmes.

title: Aga Khan University PhD in Health Sciences (Research-Based Doctoral Studies)
summary: Aga Khan University offers research-based doctoral studies in health sciences, supporting candidates in areas such as epidemiology, health systems, and population health that intersect with humanitarian and global health priorities. Admitted doctoral students typically receive funding and research support.

title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) - Graduate Degree Program
summary: The Global Korea Scholarship (formerly Korean Government Scholarship Program, KGSP) is a fully-funded scholarship by the Korean government (NIIED) supporting international students in master's and doctoral programs at Korean universities. It covers tuition, living stipend, airfare, Korean language training, and insurance, and is open to fields including public health, international development, and social sciences relevant to humanitarian and global health studies.

title: Korean Government Support Program for Foreign Students - Doctoral Research
summary: This Korean government-funded doctoral research support is administered through NIIED and participating Korean universities, providing stipends and research funding for international PhD candidates. Applicants in public health, disaster studies, migration, and international law may apply through designated host universities under the GKS framework.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) – Chinese University Program for Postgraduates
summary: This CSC doctoral scholarship stream allows Chinese universities to recruit international PhD candidates directly under the Chinese Government Scholarship framework. It offers full funding and can support research in global health, public health, international law, migration, and related interdisciplinary fields depending on the host university.

title: Taiwan ICDF Scholarship for Doctoral Studies in Disaster Management and Sustainable Development
summary: This Taiwan ICDF scholarship stream supports PhD candidates from partner nations to study disaster management, climate adaptation, and sustainable development at Taiwanese universities. It provides full financial support including tuition, living stipend, and travel, with the goal of strengthening disaster resilience in developing countries.

title: ICCR Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan (Doctoral)
summary: Under the Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan, ICCR facilitates doctoral-level scholarships for students from Commonwealth countries to pursue PhD research at Indian universities. The award generally includes tuition, stipend, and travel support, with subject areas varying by host institution and may include health, law, and social sciences relevant to humanitarian studies.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at University of Edinburgh - PhD
summary: The University of Edinburgh is a Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program partner offering fully-funded scholarships to students from Sub-Saharan Africa, including support for postgraduate and doctoral study. The program covers tuition, living costs, and additional support, with eligible fields including global health and related disciplines.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at University of Toronto - PhD
summary: The University of Toronto participates in the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, providing fully-funded scholarships to African students, with some pathways supporting graduate and doctoral-level study. The program emphasizes leadership development and covers tuition, living expenses, and travel.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at University of Cape Town - PhD
summary: The University of Cape Town is a Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program partner offering fully-funded scholarships to academically talented African students, including at postgraduate and doctoral levels. Support covers tuition, accommodation, stipends, and leadership development, with relevant fields including public health and development studies.

title: Doctoral Studentship in Crisis Management and Civil Defence
summary: The Swedish Defence University conducts research on crisis management, civil defence, and societal resilience, and periodically recruits fully-funded doctoral students in these areas. Positions are salaried employment-based PhD roles advertised on the university's website.

key_figures.name: Magnus Ranstorp
key_figures.title: Research Director, Center for Societal Security and Total Defence
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on terrorism, radicalization, and societal security, with work connecting crisis management and total defence to counterterrorism and resilience policy.

key_figures.name: Dan Öberg
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Researches military and societal crisis management, civil-military relations, and the governance of defence and emergency preparedness.

key_figures.name: Claudia Morsut
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Works on crisis management, societal security, and civil protection, including European and Nordic approaches to disaster and emergency governance.

title: Doctoral Studentship in Military History / History of War
summary: The Swedish Defence University offers fully-funded doctoral positions in Military History, covering topics related to armed conflict, warfare, and their societal consequences. These are salaried PhD positions announced periodically on the university's vacancy page.

key_figures.name: Jan Ångström
key_figures.title: Professor of War Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on war studies, military theory, and strategic studies, including the changing character of war and contemporary conflict dynamics.

key_figures.name: Magnus Petersson
key_figures.title: Professor of Military History
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on military history, intelligence studies, and Swedish defence and security policy from the early modern period to the present.

key_figures.name: Dan Öberg
key_figures.title: Associate Professor in War Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on war studies, military transformation, and the relationship between technology, organization, and the conduct of war.

title: Uppsala University Doctoral Studentships (Doktorandanställning)
summary: Uppsala University regularly advertises fully funded doctoral student positions (doktorandanställning) as salaried employment, including within departments such as Women's and Children's Health, Peace and Conflict Research, and Theology. These positions cover tuition, salary, and research costs for the duration of the PhD. Vacancies are posted continuously on the university's job portal.

key_figures.name: Peter Wallensteen
key_figures.title: Senior Professor of Peace and Conflict Research
key_figures.research_focus: Research on armed conflict, conflict resolution, and peacebuilding, including the health and humanitarian consequences of war and the conditions for sustainable peace.

key_figures.name: Mats Utas
key_figures.title: Professor of Cultural Anthropology
key_figures.research_focus: Research on conflict, humanitarian intervention, and global health in war-affected settings, with fieldwork in West Africa on youth, violence, and post-conflict recovery.

key_figures.name: Anna Mia Ekström
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Research on global health, HIV prevention, and health systems in low-resource and conflict-affected settings, with a focus on sexual and reproductive health and rights.

title: Swedish Research Council (Vetenskapsrådet) International Postdoc / Doctoral Funding
summary: The Swedish Research Council funds doctoral and postdoctoral research across disciplines, including global health, migration, and humanitarian topics, with grants often hosted at Swedish universities such as Uppsala. Funding typically covers salary and research costs for a defined project period. Applications are submitted through the council's portal with annual calls.

key_figures.name: Peter Allebeck
key_figures.title: Professor of Social Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on social epidemiology, global health, and the health consequences of conflict and displacement, including studies on mental health among refugee populations.

key_figures.name: Anna Mia Ekström
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health with emphasis on HIV, sexual and reproductive health, and health systems in low-resource and conflict-affected settings.

key_figures.name: Hans Rosling
key_figures.title: Professor of International Health (deceased 2017)
key_figures.research_focus: Pioneered global health analytics and public understanding of global development, conflict, and health trends through data visualization.

title: Uppsala University Department of Peace and Conflict Research PhD Positions
summary: The Department of Peace and Conflict Research at Uppsala University periodically advertises fully funded PhD positions focused on conflict, peacebuilding, and related humanitarian themes. Doctoral candidates are employed with a salary and receive research support. Vacancies are announced on the department and university job pages.

key_figures.name: Hans Rosling
key_figures.title: Professor of International Health (deceased 2017)
key_figures.research_focus: Global health, conflict-affected regions, and humanitarian data visualization; co-founded Gapminder and worked extensively on health in conflict and low-income settings.

key_figures.name: Peter Wallensteen
key_figures.title: Senior Professor of Peace and Conflict Research
key_figures.research_focus: Armed conflict, peace processes, and the health and humanitarian consequences of war; founder of the Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP).

key_figures.name: Ashok Swain
key_figures.title: Professor of Peace and Conflict Research
key_figures.research_focus: Forced migration, environmental and climate-induced displacement, and the humanitarian dimensions of conflict and water insecurity.

title: PhD in Political Studies - Doctoral Scholarship (University of Milan)
summary: The University of Milan funds doctoral scholarships across its PhD programmes, including Political Studies, which covers themes such as migration, humanitarianism, and international relations. Scholarships typically include a monthly stipend, tuition waiver, and research budget for the duration of the doctorate.

key_figures.name: Maurizio Ambrosini
key_figures.title: Professor of Sociology of Migration
key_figures.research_focus: Research on international migration, forced migration, asylum seekers and refugees, with attention to humanitarian governance and migrant reception policies in Italy and Europe.

key_figures.name: Elena Fiddian-Qasmiyeh
key_figures.title: Professor of Migration and Refugee Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Works on forced migration, refugee studies, humanitarianism, and Middle East displacement, including South-South humanitarian responses and refugee-host community relations.

key_figures.name: Paolo Napolitano
key_figures.title: Researcher in International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on international relations, migration governance, and humanitarian interventions, with particular attention to EU external migration policies and forced displacement.

title: PhD in Global Health and Development - Doctoral Scholarship (University of Milan)
summary: Doctoral scholarships at the University of Milan support research in global health, health systems, and related development fields. Funded PhD positions include a stipend and research allowance, with opportunities for fieldwork in humanitarian and low-resource settings.

title: PhD in Legal Studies - Doctoral Scholarship (University of Milan)
summary: The University of Milan's PhD in Legal Studies offers funded doctoral positions covering international law, human rights, and humanitarian law topics. Selected candidates receive a multi-year scholarship, tuition waiver, and research support.

key_figures.name: Chiara Ragni
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the protection of migrants and refugees, including the law of armed conflict and international criminal justice.

key_figures.name: Marco Pedrazzi
key_figures.title: Full Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on public international law, international humanitarian law, human rights, and international criminal law, with attention to armed conflicts and individual responsibility.

key_figures.name: Maurizio Arcari
key_figures.title: Full Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international law, human rights, refugee protection, and the law of international organizations, including issues related to forced migration and asylum.

title: PhD in Social and Political Sciences - Doctoral Fellowship (University of Milan)
summary: Doctoral fellowships in Social and Political Sciences at the University of Milan support research on migration, asylum, and humanitarian governance. Fellows receive a stipend, tuition coverage, and funding for research stays abroad.

title: PhD Programme in Clinical and Translational Science (Dottorato in Scienze Cliniche e Traslazionali)
summary: A doctoral programme at the University of Pisa covering clinical, translational, and public health research, with funded positions (scholarships) awarded through competitive calls. Relevant to candidates working on global health, health systems, and conflict-affected populations.

key_figures.name: Pierluigi Lopalco
key_figures.title: Full Professor of Hygiene and Preventive Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on public health, epidemiology, and vaccine-preventable diseases, with experience in international health emergency response and immunization policy.

key_figures.name: Michele Emdin
key_figures.title: Full Professor of Cardiovascular Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Investigates cardiovascular disease in global health contexts, including humanitarian cardiology and health disparities in low-resource and conflict-affected settings.

key_figures.name: Emanuele Bartolozzi
key_figures.title: Researcher in Hygiene and Public Health
key_figures.research_focus: Works on public health surveillance, health promotion, and global health governance, with attention to migrant and refugee health.

title: PhD Programme in Political Science (Dottorato in Scienze Politiche)
summary: Doctoral programme in political science at the University of Pisa offering funded PhD positions via annual competitive selection. Research areas can include migration, conflict, international institutions, and humanitarian governance.

key_figures.name: Emanuele Sommario
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the protection of persons in armed conflict and disaster situations. He has published extensively on humanitarian access, forced displacement, and the legal frameworks governing humanitarian assistance.

key_figures.name: Andrea de Guttry
key_figures.title: Full Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international humanitarian law, human rights, peacekeeping operations, and the protection of vulnerable groups including refugees and internally displaced persons. He has led major research projects on forced migration and humanitarian crises.

key_figures.name: Francesca Capone
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international human rights law, humanitarian law, and the protection of migrants and refugees, with attention to vulnerable groups and the intersection of migration and armed conflict.

title: PhD Programme in Law (Dottorato in Giurisprudenza)
summary: Doctoral programme in law at the University of Pisa with funded scholarships allocated through competitive calls. Suitable for research in international humanitarian law, human rights, and related legal fields.

key_figures.name: Emanuele Sommario
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the law of international responsibility, with particular attention to the protection of persons in armed conflict and disaster settings.

key_figures.name: Andrea de Guttry
key_figures.title: Full Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international humanitarian law, human rights law, and international security law, including peacekeeping operations, arms control, and the protection of vulnerable groups in conflict and crisis situations.

key_figures.name: Francesca Capone
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on international human rights law, international humanitarian law, and the protection of children in armed conflict, including accountability mechanisms and the rights of vulnerable persons.

title: Italian Government PhD Scholarships (Borse di studio per il Dottorato - MIUR/MUR)
summary: National PhD scholarships funded by the Italian Ministry of University and Research (MUR) and allocated to doctoral programmes at Italian universities including the University of Pisa. These cover tuition and a living stipend for the duration of the PhD.

title: PhD Programme in Earth Sciences / Environmental Sciences (Dottorato in Scienze della Terra e dell'Ambiente)
summary: Doctoral programme at the University of Pisa focused on earth and environmental sciences, including natural hazards and disaster risk. Funded positions are available through annual competitive selection.

key_figures.name: Fabio Castelli
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of Hydrology and Hydraulic Structures
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on hydrological modeling, flood forecasting, and water resources management, with applications to flood risk assessment and civil protection. He works on early warning systems and the hydrological impacts of climate variability.

key_figures.name: Enrica Caporali
key_figures.title: Professor of Hydraulic Engineering and Hydrology
key_figures.research_focus: Works on water resources management, hydrological extremes, and flood risk under climate change. Her research includes drought analysis, remote sensing for hydrology, and sustainable water management in a changing climate.

key_figures.name: Marco Lazzarotti
key_figures.title: Researcher in Geomatics and Environmental Engineering
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on geospatial analysis, remote sensing, and environmental risk mapping, including landslide and flood susceptibility assessment. His work supports disaster risk reduction through spatial modeling and Earth observation data.

title: Leiden University PhD Fellowship (Employment-based PhD positions)
summary: Leiden University regularly advertises fully-funded, salaried PhD positions (promovendi) across its faculties, including the Faculty of Governance and Global Affairs, Leiden Law School, and the Leiden University Medical Center. These are employment contracts with salary, benefits, and research/travel budget, open to international applicants. Relevant vacancies appear in humanitarian governance, global health, international law, and migration studies.

key_figures.name: Jan Pronk
key_figures.title: Professor Emeritus
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on international development, humanitarian policy, and global governance, with extensive work on conflict-affected states and United Nations peacekeeping.

key_figures.name: Larissa van den Herik
key_figures.title: Professor of Public International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international humanitarian law, international criminal law, and the legal regulation of armed conflict, including UN sanctions and counterterrorism.

key_figures.name: Thea Hilhorst
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Studies humanitarian governance, aid policy, and the everyday politics of humanitarian action in conflict and disaster settings.

title: NWO PhD in the Humanities / Social Sciences (hosted at Leiden)
summary: The Dutch Research Council (NWO) funds PhD positions through programmes such as the PhDs in the Humanities and Open Competition, which are frequently hosted at Leiden University's Faculty of Humanities and Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences. These provide full salary and research budget for the duration of the PhD, with positions advertised via Leiden.

key_figures.name: Marjaana Jauhola
key_figures.title: University Lecturer
key_figures.research_focus: Research on humanitarianism, forced migration, and gender in conflict-affected contexts, with a focus on South and Southeast Asia. She examines humanitarian governance and the politics of aid.

key_figures.name: Nadia Sonneveld
key_figures.title: University Lecturer
key_figures.research_focus: Research on international humanitarian law, human rights, and forced migration, particularly in the Middle East and North Africa. She studies legal frameworks governing displacement and humanitarian protection.

key_figures.name: Elena Fiddian-Qasmiyeh
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on forced migration, refugee studies, and humanitarianism, with a focus on the Middle East and North Africa. She examines South-South humanitarianism and refugee-host community relations.

title: Leiden-Delft-Erasmus (LDE) Joint PhD Programme
summary: The strategic alliance between Leiden University, TU Delft, and Erasmus University Rotterdam offers joint doctoral programmes, including in medical and global health topics via the LDE Centre for Global Heritage and Development and medical centres. PhD candidates receive salaried positions and interdisciplinary supervision across the three institutions.

key_figures.name: Thea Hilhorst
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Her research focuses on humanitarian aid, disaster management, and the intersection of conflict, displacement, and crisis response. She studies how humanitarian organizations and affected populations navigate complex emergencies and forced migration settings.

key_figures.name: Marleen Dekker
key_figures.title: Professor of Inclusive Development in Africa
key_figures.research_focus: Her work examines global health, poverty, and inclusive development, with attention to how crises and displacement affect vulnerable populations in low-income countries. She has published on health systems, social protection, and resilience in development contexts.

key_figures.name: Anouk Boschma
key_figures.title: Researcher and Lecturer in Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Her research addresses forced migration, humanitarian governance, and disaster response, with a focus on the politics of aid and protection of displaced populations. She works on humanitarian studies and migration-related policy questions.

title: Leiden University Medical Center (LUMC) PhD Positions
summary: LUMC, Leiden University's medical faculty, regularly recruits salaried PhD candidates for research in global health, infectious diseases, and health in crisis settings. Positions are fully funded employment contracts with supervision and training, advertised on the LUMC vacancies portal.

key_figures.name: Maria Yazdanbakhsh
key_figures.title: Professor of Immunoparasitology
key_figures.research_focus: Studies immune responses to parasitic infections and how they shape global health outcomes, with a focus on helminth infections and vaccine responses in low- and middle-income countries.

key_figures.name: Ria Reis
key_figures.title: Professor of Medical Anthropology
key_figures.research_focus: Examines health, illness, and care in contexts of adversity, including conflict-affected and disaster-prone settings, with attention to global health and community resilience.

key_figures.name: Joris van der Kruk
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Researches humanitarian action, conflict health, and disaster management, focusing on aid effectiveness and health system resilience in crisis settings.

title: LeidenASA / Leiden African Studies Centre PhD Scholarships
summary: The African Studies Centre Leiden (part of Leiden University) hosts PhD candidates researching African development, migration, and humanitarian issues, often funded through NWO, Leiden University, or external fellowships. Candidates receive supervision, workspace, and access to Leiden's research community.

key_figures.name: Marja Spierenburg
key_figures.title: Professor of Anthropology of Sustainable Development and Globalization
key_figures.research_focus: Research on land governance, displacement, and the politics of development, including forced migration linked to large-scale land acquisitions and conservation.

key_figures.name: Anouk Boschma
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Works on humanitarian governance, aid policy, and the politics of humanitarian intervention, with attention to displacement and crisis response.

key_figures.name: Ruth Kutalek
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Medical anthropology and global health research focusing on migration, health equity, and access to care for displaced and marginalized populations.

title: Utrecht University Doctoral Grant (PhD Fellowship)
summary: Utrecht University offers funded doctoral positions in which PhD candidates are appointed as employees with a competitive salary, pension, and holiday allowance for the duration of the research. These positions are embedded in research groups such as the Utrecht Centre for Global Challenges and the Julius Center for Health Sciences and Primary Care. Openings are announced via the university's vacancy portal.

key_figures.name: Diederik van de Beek
key_figures.title: Professor of Neurology
key_figures.research_focus: Global health and infectious disease research, including meningitis and emerging infections, with collaborations in low-resource settings.

key_figures.name: Thea Hilhorst
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Humanitarian studies, aid policy, and the intersection of humanitarian action with development and peacebuilding.

key_figures.name: Cedric Ryngaert
key_figures.title: Professor of Public International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Public international law, including international humanitarian law, jurisdiction, and accountability for international crimes.

title: Utrecht University / Netherlands Government Holland Scholarship for International PhD Candidates
summary: The Holland Scholarship is a Dutch national scholarship for international students from outside the EEA, administered in part through Dutch universities including Utrecht University. It is primarily aimed at bachelor's and master's students, but some doctoral candidates may access related national funding streams. It provides a one-time grant rather than full PhD funding.

key_figures.name: Juliette Mattijssen
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on global health governance, health systems strengthening, and the politics of global health, with attention to equity and access in low- and middle-income countries.

key_figures.name: Dirk-Jan Koch
key_figures.title: Professor by Special Appointment
key_figures.research_focus: Works on humanitarian aid, international cooperation, and the effectiveness of development and humanitarian interventions, including disaster response and aid policy.

key_figures.name: Thea Hilhorst
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Leading scholar in humanitarian studies, disaster management, and conflict-related crises, focusing on humanitarian governance, resilience, and aid practices in fragile settings.

title: Utrecht Centre for Global Challenges PhD Fellowships
summary: The Utrecht Centre for Global Challenges (UGlobe) at Utrecht University supports interdisciplinary research on global issues including conflict, migration, and global health, and periodically hosts or co-funds PhD researchers. Fellowships are tied to specific funded projects and advertised through the centre and university vacancy pages. Funding typically covers a full doctoral salary for the project duration.

key_figures.name: Juliette van der Kwaak
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on sexual and reproductive health and rights in humanitarian settings, with a focus on conflict-affected populations and health system strengthening.

key_figures.name: Diana M. J. Delnoij
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Health services research and global health governance, including access to care in fragile and conflict-affected settings.

key_figures.name: Ruben van der Hoeven
key_figures.title: Researcher
key_figures.research_focus: Humanitarian studies and conflict health, examining health interventions and humanitarian coordination in crisis contexts.

title: Amsterdam School for Cultural Analysis (ASCA) PhD Fellowship
summary: ASCA hosts PhD candidates in cultural analysis, including projects on migration, displacement, and humanitarianism. Funded positions are offered through periodic calls with salary and research support.

key_figures.name: Elena Fiddian-Qasmiyeh
key_figures.title: Professor of Migration and Refugee Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Her work examines forced migration, refugee studies, and humanitarian responses, with particular attention to the Middle East and North Africa. She also explores cultural and religious dimensions of displacement and refugee-led humanitarianism.

key_figures.name: Mieke Bal
key_figures.title: Professor Emerita of Cultural Analysis
key_figures.research_focus: A foundational figure in cultural analysis, her work addresses migration, exile, and displacement through visual culture, film, and critical theory. She has written extensively on the cultural politics of mobility and belonging.

key_figures.name: Polly Pallister-Wilkins
key_figures.title: Associate Professor in Conflict Resolution and Governance
key_figures.research_focus: She researches humanitarianism, border politics, and forced migration, focusing on humanitarian borderwork and the politics of rescue in the Mediterranean. Her work bridges humanitarian studies and critical migration scholarship.

title: UvA Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences PhD Positions
summary: The UvA Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences regularly advertises fully-funded PhD positions, including on migration, refugee studies, and humanitarian governance. Positions are salaried employment contracts for four years.

key_figures.name: Willemijn Verkoren
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on conflict, peacebuilding, and development, with attention to fragile states and the consequences of violent conflict for societies and governance.

key_figures.name: Marleen Dekker
key_figures.title: Professor by Special Appointment
key_figures.research_focus: Works on inclusive development, poverty, and vulnerability in conflict-affected and low-income settings, including forced migration and humanitarian policy.

key_figures.name: Darshan Vigneswaran
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Researches migration governance, borders, and forced displacement, with a focus on how states and international institutions manage mobility and protection.

title: Amsterdam UMC Doctoral Positions in Global and Conflict Health
summary: Amsterdam UMC, affiliated with UvA, offers doctoral positions in global health, infectious diseases, and health in humanitarian settings. PhD candidates receive salaried contracts and research support.

key_figures.name: Joost B. L. Hoekstra
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on global health governance, health systems strengthening, and the intersection of global health with conflict and humanitarian crises.

key_figures.name: Marleen Temmerman
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Research addresses sexual and reproductive health in humanitarian settings, health systems in fragile states, and global health policy.

key_figures.name: Dirk-Jan Koch
key_figures.title: Professor by Special Appointment of International Development Cooperation
key_figures.research_focus: Examines aid effectiveness, humanitarian assistance in conflict-affected areas, and disaster response governance.

title: Amsterdam Institute for Global Health and Development (AIGHD) PhD Fellowships
