title: University of Canterbury Brownlie Scholarship
summary: The Brownlie Scholarship is a prestigious doctoral scholarship at the University of Canterbury awarded to outstanding PhD candidates. It provides full fees and a generous stipend and is open across disciplines, including health, humanitarian, and disaster-related research.

title: HCRI Doctoral Studentships (Humanitarian and Conflict Response Institute)
summary: The Humanitarian and Conflict Response Institute (HCRI) at the University of Manchester hosts PhD researchers in humanitarian studies, conflict health, disaster management, and forced migration. Funded studentships are periodically advertised through HCRI and its partner schools, often covering fees and stipend for UK and international candidates.

key_figures.name: Rony Brauman
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on humanitarian action, medical ethics in conflict, and the politics of aid. Has written extensively on humanitarian intervention and the dilemmas of relief work in war zones.

key_figures.name: Peter Redfield
key_figures.title: Professor of Anthropology
key_figures.research_focus: Examines humanitarianism, global health, and the moral dimensions of aid. His work includes ethnographic studies of Médecins Sans Frontières and the politics of life in crisis settings.

key_figures.name: Bertrand Taithe
key_figures.title: Professor of Cultural History
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the history of humanitarianism, conflict medicine, and disaster relief. He leads projects on the historical evolution of humanitarian aid and medical interventions in crises.

title: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships (hosted at University of Manchester)
summary: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships are funded by the UK government and can be hosted at the University of Manchester for candidates from low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries. They cover tuition fees, stipend, and travel, and support research in development-related fields including global health, humanitarian studies, and migration.

key_figures.name: Mukesh Kapila
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Humanitarian Affairs
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health policy, humanitarian crises, conflict and atrocity prevention, with extensive experience in international humanitarian response and forced displacement contexts.

key_figures.name: Jenny Peterson
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer in Human Geography
key_figures.research_focus: Researches forced migration, displacement, humanitarianism, and the politics of aid, with a focus on refugee protection and global humanitarian governance.

key_figures.name: Tanja Müller
key_figures.title: Professor of Political Sociology
key_figures.research_focus: Examines forced migration, refugee livelihoods, humanitarianism, and global development, particularly in African contexts and protracted displacement situations.

title: King's College London PhD Studentships (Health Sciences / Global Health)
summary: King's College London offers a range of competitively awarded PhD studentships across its faculties, including the Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine and the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience, covering fees and a stipend. These support doctoral research in global health, conflict and health, and related public health fields.

key_figures.name: Richard Sullivan
key_figures.title: Professor of Cancer and Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on global health systems, cancer care in low- and middle-income countries, and health in conflict-affected settings. Directs the Institute of Cancer Policy and works on humanitarian health and health system strengthening.

key_figures.name: Preeti Patel
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Researches health systems in conflict-affected and fragile states, global health governance, and humanitarian response. Leads the Conflict and Health Research Group at King's College London.

key_figures.name: Simon Wessely
key_figures.title: Professor of Psychological Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Studies the health effects of military service, conflict, and terrorism, including mental health of veterans and emergency responders. Former President of the Royal College of Psychiatrists.

title: King's College London Centre for Doctoral Training / LISS DTP Studentships (ESRC)
summary: The London Interdisciplinary Social Science Doctoral Training Partnership (LISS DTP), funded by the ESRC and hosted partly at King's College London, provides fully-funded studentships for doctoral research in the social sciences. Relevant research areas include forced migration, humanitarian studies, and conflict-related social research.

key_figures.name: Jenny Phillimore
key_figures.title: Professor of Migration and Superdiversity
key_figures.research_focus: Research on migration, refugee integration, and superdiversity, with a focus on the experiences of forced migrants and the local governance of migration. She leads major projects on refugee settlement and integration in the UK and Europe.

key_figures.name: Khalid Koser
key_figures.title: Professor of Migration and Security
key_figures.research_focus: Research on forced migration, refugee protection, and the intersection of migration with security and development. He has published extensively on asylum, internal displacement, and humanitarian responses to migration crises.

key_figures.name: Elena Fiddian-Qasmiyeh
key_figures.title: Professor of Migration and Refugee Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Research on forced migration, refugee studies, and humanitarianism, with particular attention to gender, religion, and South-South displacement. She has led major projects on refugee-host relations and faith-based humanitarianism.

title: King's College London War Studies PhD Studentships
summary: The Department of War Studies at King's College London, a leading centre for conflict and security research, offers PhD studentships supporting doctoral work in areas such as international humanitarian law, conflict, and humanitarian studies. Awards typically cover tuition fees and provide a maintenance stipend.

key_figures.name: Guglielmo Verdirame
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international law, human rights, and the laws of armed conflict, with particular attention to humanitarian access and the legal regulation of conflict.

key_figures.name: Rebecca Sutton
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer in International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the protection of civilians in armed conflict.

key_figures.name: Mats Berdal
key_figures.title: Professor of Security and Development
key_figures.research_focus: Studies civil wars, conflict resolution, peacebuilding, and the political economy of armed conflict, with a focus on humanitarian dimensions of war.

title: King's College London PGR International Scholarships
summary: King's College London offers a range of postgraduate research scholarships for international students, providing fee support or partial funding for doctoral study. These can be applied to research in global health, humanitarian studies, and forced migration within relevant departments.

key_figures.name: Richard Sullivan
key_figures.title: Professor of Cancer and Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on global health systems, health in conflict and humanitarian settings, and the interface between health, security, and development. His work addresses cancer care in low- and middle-income countries and health system strengthening in fragile states.

key_figures.name: Preeti Patel
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the intersections of global health, conflict, and forced migration, including health system resilience in conflict-affected states and humanitarian responses to displacement. She leads work on health diplomacy and the politics of humanitarian aid.

key_figures.name: Fouad M. Fouad
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer in Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Works on health in humanitarian crises and forced migration, with a focus on the Syrian conflict and refugee health in the Middle East. His research examines health systems, access to care, and the politics of humanitarian health interventions.

title: King's College London Health & Social Care Research Studentships (NIHR-linked)
summary: King's College London, in partnership with health research funders such as the NIHR, offers doctoral studentships in health and social care research. These support PhD projects relevant to global health, conflict and health, and health systems in crisis and disaster settings.

key_figures.name: Richard Sullivan
key_figures.title: Professor of Cancer and Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on global health systems, health in conflict and humanitarian settings, and the delivery of health services in fragile and crisis-affected states. His work spans cancer care in low-resource settings, health security, and the intersection of conflict, disasters, and public health.

key_figures.name: Preeti Patel
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the health impacts of conflict and forced displacement, global health governance, and humanitarian health responses. Her work examines how war, sanctions, and political instability shape health systems and access to care in conflict-affected regions.

key_figures.name: Virginia Murray
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Disaster Risk Reduction
key_figures.research_focus: Works on disaster risk reduction, emergency preparedness, and the health dimensions of climate-related and natural disasters. She has contributed to international frameworks on disaster risk management and public health emergency response.

title: LSE Law Department PhD Studentship
summary: The LSE Law Department offers funded PhD studentships for doctoral research, including projects in international law, human rights and international humanitarian law. Studentships generally cover full fees and a stipend and are awarded on a competitive basis.

key_figures.name: Christine Chinkin
key_figures.title: Emeritus Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Her work addresses international human rights law, international humanitarian law, and gender perspectives on armed conflict, including landmark analysis of the gendered dimensions of conflict and peace processes.

key_figures.name: Chaloka Beyani
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: He researches international human rights law, humanitarian law, and forced displacement, with particular attention to the protection of internally displaced persons and conflict-affected populations.

key_figures.name: Kirsten Ainley
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Her research examines international criminal law, human rights, and humanitarian intervention, focusing on the politics and ethics of international justice and protection in conflict settings.

title: LSE Middle East Centre / Regional Research PhD Funding
summary: LSE research centres such as the Middle East Centre and the Firoz Lalji Institute for Africa offer grants and partial funding to support PhD fieldwork and research on conflict, displacement and humanitarian issues. These complement central LSE studentships and are awarded competitively.

key_figures.name: Michael Bloom
key_figures.title: Visiting Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on forced migration, refugee health, and humanitarian response, with a focus on displacement and health outcomes in conflict-affected populations.

key_figures.name: Bayard Roberts
key_figures.title: Professor of Health Policy and Systems
key_figures.research_focus: Research on health systems and policy in conflict-affected and humanitarian settings, including forced migration and refugee health.

key_figures.name: Kirsten Ainley
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Research on international relations, human rights, and humanitarian intervention, including the politics of forced migration and conflict.

title: FindAPhD PhD Studentships in Conflict and Health Research
summary: FindAPhD hosts listings for fully-funded doctoral research in conflict and health, often linked to humanitarian research centres and global health institutes. These studentships are funded by research councils, charities, or university schemes. Applications are made to the specific host university.

title: DAAD Doctoral Scholarships for Students from Developing Countries
summary: This DAAD programme funds doctoral candidates from developing and emerging countries to complete a PhD at a German university. It covers monthly stipends, health insurance, travel costs, and study and research allowances. Fields such as global health, humanitarian action, and forced migration are eligible when a German host institution accepts the applicant.

title: Campus France Doctoral Scholarships (Bourses de Doctorat)
summary: Campus France administers various doctoral scholarship programs for international students wishing to pursue a PhD in France, often in partnership with French embassies and research institutions. These scholarships typically cover tuition, monthly living stipend, travel, and health insurance for the duration of the doctoral program.

title: French Government Scholarships (BGF) for Doctoral Studies
summary: The French Government Scholarships (Bourses du Gouvernement Français) are awarded through French embassies and administered with Campus France support. They fund international PhD students in priority research areas, which can include humanitarian and global health topics, covering stipend, travel, and insurance.

title: Finnish Government Scholarship Pool (Doctoral Level)
summary: The Finnish Government Scholarship Pool, administered by EDUFI, offers doctoral-level grants to international students and researchers for study and research at Finnish universities. It supports fields including global health, humanitarian studies, and forced migration research.

title: Copenhagen Graduate School of Global Health PhD Scholarship
summary: The Copenhagen Graduate School of Global Health at the University of Copenhagen offers fully-funded PhD positions within global health research, including topics related to conflict-affected populations, health systems in fragile settings, and humanitarian health. PhD fellows receive a salary, travel budget, and research costs for a three-year programme.

key_figures.name: Flemming Konradsen
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on global health, environmental health, and health in low-income settings, including water, sanitation, and injury prevention. He has led international collaborations on public health challenges in resource-poor and conflict-affected contexts.

key_figures.name: Ib Christian Bygbjerg
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health and Infectious Diseases
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health, infectious diseases, and maternal-child health, with emphasis on health systems in low-resource settings. His research includes diabetes, malaria, and public health interventions in vulnerable populations.

key_figures.name: Peter Aaby
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Conducts research on global health, vaccines, and child survival in low-income countries, particularly in Guinea-Bissau. His work has influenced understanding of non-specific effects of vaccines and public health in conflict-affected and resource-limited settings.

title: Danish Research Council (DFF) PhD Fellowship at University of Copenhagen
summary: The Independent Research Fund Denmark (Danmarks Frie Forskningsfond) funds PhD fellowships hosted at Danish universities including the University of Copenhagen. Projects in humanitarian studies, forced migration, and global health can be funded through this scheme, covering salary and research expenses for up to three years.

key_figures.name: Anja Kublitz
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Anthropological research on forced migration, refugee families, and transnational kinship, with a focus on Palestinian refugees and humanitarian governance in the Middle East and Denmark.

key_figures.name: Zachary Whyte
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on refugee reception, asylum systems, and the everyday governance of forced migration in Denmark and Europe, with attention to humanitarian practices and integration policies.

key_figures.name: Flemming Konradsen
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Global health researcher focusing on health in humanitarian crises, disaster response, and the health of displaced populations, with extensive work in low-resource and conflict-affected settings.

title: University of Copenhagen PhD Scholarship (Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences)
summary: The Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences at the University of Copenhagen regularly advertises fully-funded three-year PhD scholarships. Research areas include global health, disaster medicine, and health in humanitarian crises, with positions salaried according to Danish state collective agreements.

key_figures.name: Peter Aaby
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Research on global health, particularly in low-income countries, focusing on measles, vitamin A, and nonspecific effects of vaccines. Also works on health interventions in conflict-affected and resource-poor settings.

key_figures.name: Flemming Konradsen
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on global health, disaster management, and health in humanitarian crises, including water, sanitation, and vector-borne diseases in low-resource settings.

key_figures.name: Jens Seeberg
key_figures.title: Professor, Anthropology of Health
key_figures.research_focus: Research on global health, conflict-affected populations, and health systems in fragile settings, with a focus on medical anthropology and humanitarian interventions.

title: Danish Institute for International Studies (DIIS) PhD Fellowship
summary: DIIS, in collaboration with the University of Copenhagen, hosts PhD fellows working on humanitarian studies, forced migration, and conflict-related research. Fellows are enrolled at the university and funded through institutional or research council grants for three years.

key_figures.name: Anja Kublitz
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Anthropological research on forced migration, refugee families, and the everyday lives of people displaced by conflict, with a focus on Denmark and the Middle East.

key_figures.name: Morten Skovdal
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on the social and community dimensions of health in humanitarian and forced migration contexts, including HIV, mental health, and child well-being in sub-Saharan Africa.

key_figures.name: Peter Vedel Kessing
key_figures.title: Senior Researcher
key_figures.research_focus: Legal and human rights research on migration control, refugee protection, and the intersection of humanitarian law with forced displacement and conflict.

title: Danish Council for Independent Research – Sapere Aude PhD Grant
summary: The Sapere Aude programme under the Independent Research Fund Denmark supports excellent research projects that can include PhD fellowships at the University of Copenhagen. Topics in humanitarian studies, global health, and forced migration are eligible, with full salary and research costs covered.

key_figures.name: Peter Vedel Kessing
key_figures.title: Senior Researcher
key_figures.research_focus: Research on migration law, human rights, and the legal dimensions of forced migration and humanitarian protection.

key_figures.name: Anja Kublitz
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Anthropological research on forced migration, refugee studies, and humanitarianism in the Middle East and Denmark.

key_figures.name: Flemming Konradsen
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Global health research with focus on humanitarian crises, disaster response, and health in low-resource and conflict-affected settings.

title: University of Copenhagen – Department of Anthropology PhD Scholarship
summary: The Department of Anthropology at the University of Copenhagen offers fully-funded PhD scholarships, including research on humanitarianism, forced migration, and disaster response. PhD fellows receive a monthly salary and research budget for a three-year period.

key_figures.name: Anja Kublitz
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Anthropological research on forced migration, refugee families, and transnational kinship, with a focus on Palestinian refugees in Denmark and the Middle East.

key_figures.name: Nauja Kleist
key_figures.title: Senior Researcher
key_figures.research_focus: Research on migration, diaspora, humanitarianism, and development, particularly Somali transnational networks and the politics of humanitarian aid.

key_figures.name: Peter Kjær Mackie Jensen
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on disaster management, humanitarian emergencies, and public health in low-income settings, including cholera and diarrheal disease control in disaster-affected populations.

title: Croatian Government Scholarship for Foreign Students (Bilateral/Multilateral Programme)
summary: The Ministry of Science and Education of Croatia offers scholarships to foreign students, including doctoral candidates, under bilateral and multilateral cooperation programmes. Awards typically cover tuition, monthly stipend, accommodation, and health insurance for the duration of study at Croatian public universities.

title: Croatian Government Scholarship for Croatian Diaspora / Croatian National Minority Students
summary: The Central State Office for Croats Abroad and the Ministry of Science and Education provide scholarships for members of the Croatian diaspora and national minorities, which can support doctoral studies at Croatian universities. Funding typically covers tuition and a stipend for eligible candidates.

title: Erasmus+ Doctoral Mobility / Joint Doctorates hosted at Croatian Universities
summary: Erasmus+ supports doctoral candidates through mobility grants and joint doctorate programmes involving Croatian universities as partners. These fund research stays, tuition, and living costs for PhD candidates working on topics such as migration, health, and disaster response.

title: Croatian Ministry of Science and Education State Scholarship for STEM and Priority Fields
summary: The Ministry of Science and Education awards state scholarships to doctoral students in priority and STEM fields at Croatian universities. The scholarship provides a monthly stipend to support doctoral research, with eligibility determined by annual calls.

title: Qatar Foundation WISE Doctoral Fellowship
summary: The World Innovation Summit for Education (WISE) is a Qatar Foundation initiative that supports research and doctoral-level work related to education in crisis and conflict settings, including displaced populations. WISE fellowships and research grants support scholars examining education, humanitarian response, and migration.

title: Sidra Medicine Doctoral Research Fellowship
summary: Sidra Medicine, a Qatar Foundation member, offers doctoral research training opportunities in biomedical and clinical research, including maternal and child health relevant to conflict and humanitarian settings. Fellows receive full funding, mentorship, and access to Sidra's research facilities.

title: Fogarty International Research Training Grants (D43) - Global Infectious Diseases
summary: Fogarty's D43 research training grants support institutional partnerships that train doctoral and postdoctoral scientists in global infectious disease research. These grants fund trainees at LMIC institutions and are not direct PhD scholarships for study in the United States.

title: Aga Khan University PhD Fellowships in Health Sciences
summary: Aga Khan University offers fully-funded PhD fellowships in health sciences through its graduate programmes, supporting doctoral research in public health, epidemiology, and health systems. These fellowships are aimed at strengthening health research capacity in Pakistan and the wider region, including areas relevant to humanitarian and conflict-affected settings.

key_figures.name: Zulfiqar A. Bhutta
key_figures.title: Distinguished University Professor and Founding Director, Centre of Excellence in Women and Child Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global maternal, newborn, and child health, with extensive work on nutrition, evidence-based interventions, and health in conflict-affected and low-resource settings.

key_figures.name: Sana Sheikh
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor, Department of Community Health Sciences
key_figures.research_focus: Public health and global health research, including maternal and child health, health systems strengthening, and community-based interventions in Pakistan and other low-resource settings.

key_figures.name: Asad Mian
key_figures.title: Professor, Department of Emergency Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Emergency medicine, global health, and health in humanitarian and conflict settings, with a focus on innovation, capacity building, and emergency care systems.

title: Aga Khan University Institute for Human Development PhD Programme
summary: The Institute for Human Development at Aga Khan University hosts doctoral research focused on early childhood development, human development, and related social determinants of health. The programme supports research relevant to vulnerable populations, including displaced and conflict-affected communities.

title: Aga Khan University PhD in Public Health (Community Health Sciences)
summary: The Department of Community Health Sciences at Aga Khan University offers doctoral training in public health with research themes spanning disaster preparedness, health in humanitarian emergencies, and population health. Funded PhD positions are available for qualified candidates, particularly those addressing health challenges in low-resource and crisis settings.

key_figures.name: Zulfiqar A. Bhutta
key_figures.title: Professor and Chair, Department of Paediatrics and Child Health; Founding Director, Centre of Excellence in Women and Child Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global maternal, newborn, and child health, with extensive work on health systems in fragile and conflict-affected settings and humanitarian emergencies.

key_figures.name: Asad Iqbal Mian
key_figures.title: Associate Professor, Department of Emergency Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Emergency medicine and disaster preparedness, including mass casualty management and prehospital emergency care systems in low-resource and disaster-affected settings.

key_figures.name: Sana Gul
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor, Department of Community Health Sciences
key_figures.research_focus: Global health and humanitarian response, focusing on reproductive health and health service delivery in conflict-affected and displaced populations.

title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) - Graduate Degree Program
university: KGSP Korea (National Institute for International Education, Ministry of Education)
summary: The Global Korea Scholarship (formerly Korean Government Scholarship Program, KGSP) is a fully-funded Korean government scholarship for international students pursuing master's and doctoral degrees at Korean universities. It covers tuition, living stipend, airfare, Korean language training, and settlement allowance. Applicants may pursue fields relevant to global health, development, and humanitarian studies depending on the host university's available programs.

title: Korea Foundation for Advanced Studies (KFAS) Doctoral Fellowship
university: KGSP Korea (Korea Foundation for Advanced Studies)
summary: KFAS offers doctoral fellowships supporting outstanding scholars in Korea and abroad, including support for overseas doctoral study by Korean nationals and some international collaborative programs. Fields can include social sciences, public policy, and health-related disciplines depending on annual priorities. Funding typically covers tuition, living expenses, and research costs.

title: Korean Government Support Program for Foreign Students (GKS) - Partner University Doctoral Track
summary: Under the GKS program, designated Korean universities host international doctoral candidates in various disciplines including public health, international law, and development studies. The scholarship provides full tuition, monthly stipend, Korean language training, and travel support. Applicants apply through either the embassy track or university track depending on the host institution.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship (CSC) – Chinese University Program for Doctoral Students
summary: This CSC doctoral funding route allows international applicants to apply directly to participating Chinese universities for fully funded PhD positions. Fields such as global health, public health, migration studies, and humanitarian research may be supported where the university offers relevant doctoral programs and supervisors.

title: CSC – Chinese Government Special Scholarship for International Students
summary: The Chinese Government Special Scholarship supports international students, including doctoral candidates, at selected Chinese institutions. It generally provides full funding for tuition, living costs, accommodation, and insurance, and can be used for health, law, development, and disaster-related doctoral research where available.

title: CSC – High-Level University Graduate Program
summary: The CSC High-Level University Graduate Program funds doctoral students at participating Chinese universities as part of China’s international education initiatives. It typically covers tuition, stipend, accommodation, and insurance, and may support research in global health, development, and related interdisciplinary fields.

title: Taiwan ICDF Scholarship - Doctoral Studies in Disaster Management and Related Fields
summary: Taiwan ICDF supports PhD-level study in disaster management and related fields such as environmental engineering and climate resilience at selected Taiwanese universities. This is part of the broader ICDF Higher Education Scholarship Program aimed at capacity building in partner developing nations.

title: ICCR Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan (Doctoral Research in India)
summary: Under the Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan, ICCR facilitates doctoral research placements at Indian institutions for eligible Commonwealth candidates. The award supports tuition and maintenance, and can be used for research in global health, humanitarian response, and disaster management.

title: ICCR Scholarship for Afghan Nationals (PhD Studies in India)
summary: ICCR offers dedicated scholarship slots for Afghan nationals, including doctoral-level study at Indian universities. The scheme covers tuition and living expenses and can support PhD research relevant to humanitarian studies, public health, and displacement.

title: ICCR Scholarship for African Students (PhD Research in India)
summary: ICCR administers scholarship programs for African students, including doctoral research at Indian universities. Funding typically includes tuition and a stipend, and candidates may pursue PhD topics in global health, humanitarian studies, and disaster management.

title: Chevening Scholarships (Master's level, not PhD)
summary: Chevening Scholarships are the UK government's international awards scheme, funded by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office and partner organisations. They fund one-year master's degrees in the UK, not PhDs, so they are not a doctoral funding route. Relevant fields such as global health, humanitarian studies, and forced migration can be pursued at master's level only.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at McGill University - PhD
summary: McGill University partners with the Mastercard Foundation to offer fully-funded scholarships to students from Sub-Saharan Africa, including doctoral candidates. The program supports graduate studies across disciplines with relevance to humanitarian studies, global health, and forced migration. Funding includes tuition, living stipend, travel, and academic support.

title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at African Leadership University - PhD
summary: The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at African Leadership University supports talented African students with fully-funded scholarships. While ALU's primary focus is undergraduate and master's level, the broader Mastercard Foundation Scholars network includes doctoral pathways at select partner institutions. The program emphasizes leadership development and social impact across Africa.

title: Doctoral Studentship in International Law / International Humanitarian Law
summary: The Swedish Defence University hosts research and doctoral training in international law, including international humanitarian law, through its law subject area. Fully-funded salaried doctoral positions are advertised when available.

key_figures.name: Ove Bring
key_figures.title: Professor Emeritus of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international law, international humanitarian law, and the law of armed conflict, with extensive scholarship on the laws of war and human rights.

key_figures.name: Pål Wrange
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international law, the use of force, international humanitarian law, and the legal regulation of armed conflict.

key_figures.name: Cecilia Tengroth
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer in International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on international humanitarian law, human rights law, and legal issues related to armed conflict and military operations.

title: Uppsala University Department of Peace and Conflict Research PhD Programme
summary: The Department of Peace and Conflict Research at Uppsala University offers a fully funded PhD programme with salaried doctoral positions. Research areas include conflict dynamics, humanitarian consequences of war, and forced displacement. Positions are advertised periodically and include full salary and research support.

key_figures.name: Hans Rosling
key_figures.title: Professor of International Health (deceased 2017)
key_figures.research_focus: Global health, conflict-affected populations, and humanitarian epidemiology; known for Gapminder and work on health in complex emergencies.

key_figures.name: Ashok Swain
key_figures.title: Professor of Peace and Conflict Research
key_figures.research_focus: Environmental and water conflicts, forced migration, and the politics of humanitarian crises in South Asia and beyond.

key_figures.name: Kristina Hedlund
key_figures.title: Researcher, Department of Women's and Children's Health
key_figures.research_focus: Sexual and reproductive health in humanitarian settings, conflict-affected populations, and forced migration health outcomes.

title: Uppsala University Department of Theology PhD Position in Humanitarian Studies / Ethics
summary: The Department of Theology at Uppsala University, home to research in ethics, human rights, and humanitarianism, periodically offers fully funded doctoral positions. Research may relate to humanitarian ethics, migration, and international law. Positions are salaried and advertised on the university's vacancy portal.

key_figures.name: Rebecca Stern
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the legal regulation of armed conflict, including humanitarian access and protection of civilians.

key_figures.name: Kristoffer Lidén
key_figures.title: Senior Researcher
key_figures.research_focus: Works on humanitarian studies, humanitarian ethics, and the politics of humanitarian intervention, with attention to forced migration and conflict-affected populations.

key_figures.name: Maja Janmyr
key_figures.title: Professor of International Migration Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches forced migration, refugee law, and international legal frameworks governing displacement, with a focus on the Middle East and humanitarian protection.

title: PhD in Sociology and Social Research - Doctoral Scholarship (University of Milan)
summary: Doctoral scholarships in Sociology and Social Research at the University of Milan support empirical work on migration, humanitarian action, and social responses to crises. The funding includes a stipend, tuition waiver, and research allowance.

title: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAECI) Scholarships for Foreign Students
summary: Scholarships offered by the Italian government to international students, usable for doctoral study at Italian universities including the University of Pisa. They cover tuition, a monthly stipend and health insurance for the duration of the programme.

title: University of Pisa PhD Scholarships (Borse di Dottorato)
summary: The University of Pisa awards fully-funded PhD scholarships each year through its competitive doctoral admission calls across all its doctoral programmes. These cover a monthly stipend, tuition waiver and research budget, and are open to international applicants in fields including global health, migration and humanitarian studies.

title: Leiden University PhD Fellowship (Doctoral Position Funding)
summary: Leiden University regularly advertises fully-funded salaried PhD positions (promovendi) across its faculties, including the Faculty of Governance and Global Affairs and Leiden University Medical Center. These are employment-based doctoral positions open to international applicants, with topics varying by project. Relevant research is conducted at institutes such as the Institute of Security and Global Affairs and the Leiden University Centre for International Relations.

key_figures.name: Jan Pronk
key_figures.title: Professor Emeritus
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on international development, humanitarian action, and global governance, with extensive experience in UN peacekeeping and humanitarian policy.

key_figures.name: Larissa van den Herik
key_figures.title: Professor of Public International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international humanitarian law, international criminal law, and the legal regulation of armed conflict, including UN sanctions and counterterrorism.

key_figures.name: Thea Hilhorst

title: Monash Humanitarian Scholarship
summary: The Monash Humanitarian Scholarship supports students from refugee or asylum-seeker backgrounds, including those pursuing higher degrees by research, by covering tuition fees and providing a stipend. It is aimed at applicants whose studies relate to humanitarian and forced migration issues.

key_figures.name: Professor Susan Kneebone

key_figures.name: Associate Professor Marie Segrave

title: Otago Global Health Institute (OGHI) PhD Scholarship
summary: The Otago Global Health Institute supports doctoral research in global health through scholarships and research funding for projects addressing health inequities, infectious diseases, and health systems in low-resource settings. Funding typically covers fees and stipend for successful applicants.

key_figures.title: Professor of International Health

key_figures.name: Michael Baker

key_figures.name: Joanne Baxter
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of Public Health

title: University of Otago Postgraduate Scholarship (Master's and PhD)
summary: The University of Otago offers a range of postgraduate scholarships that provide partial or full funding for doctoral study across disciplines, including social sciences, law, and health. These are awarded on academic merit and can support research relevant to humanitarian and forced migration studies.

key_figures.name: Carol Farbotko

key_figures.name: Suzanne Phibbs

title: Victoria University of Wellington Doctoral Scholarship (Vice-Chancellor's Strategic Research Scholarships)
summary: Strategic Research Scholarships are awarded to outstanding doctoral candidates working in areas aligned with the university's strategic research priorities, which have included health, wellbeing, and social policy. They typically cover tuition fees and provide a living stipend for the duration of the PhD.

title: Health Research Council of New Zealand Māori Health Research PhD Scholarship
summary: The Health Research Council of New Zealand funds PhD scholarships, including Māori Health Research scholarships, that can be hosted at the University of Auckland. They support doctoral research in health, including public and global health topics, with a stipend and fees.

key_figures.name: Bridget Kool

key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on Pacific health, health equity, and the social determinants of health for Pacific peoples in New Zealand. Her work addresses ethnic disparities in health outcomes and culturally appropriate health interventions.

title: Marsden Fund Doctoral Scholarship
summary: Marsden Fund grants, administered by Royal Society Te Apārangi, often include funding for doctoral scholarships attached to funded research projects at New Zealand universities including the University of Auckland. These can support PhD research in social sciences, law, and humanities relevant to humanitarian studies and forced migration.

key_figures.name: Jay Marlowe

title: Health Research Council of New Zealand Doctoral Scholarship

title: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships (for least developed countries and low/middle income countries)

summary: Chevening Scholarships are UK government-funded awards for international students, primarily for master's degrees, though some doctoral funding may be available in specific cases. title: King's College London PhD Studentships (Graduate School Studentship Scheme)
summary: King's College London offers competitive PhD studentships through its Graduate School and individual faculties, covering tuition fees and providing a stipend for living costs. title: King's College London Centre for Doctoral Training / London Interdisciplinary Doctoral Programme (LIDo) Studentships

key_figures.name: Preeti Patel
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the intersection of global health, conflict, and humanitarian response, including health system resilience in conflict-affected settings and the politics of humanitarian aid. Leads research at the Conflict and Health Research Group.

key_figures.name: Gemma Bowsher

key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health security, disaster and emergency response, and the health impacts of conflict and complex emergencies. Her research addresses humanitarian health governance and crisis preparedness.

title: King's College London War Studies / Conflict and Health PhD Funding
summary: King's College London, home to the Department of War Studies and the King's Centre for Global Health and Health Partnerships, offers funded PhD opportunities in conflict, humanitarian, and health-related research. Funding typically covers fees and stipend, awarded competitively through faculty or project-specific schemes.

key_figures.name: Preeti Patel
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Conflict

key_figures.name: Rebecca Sutton

title: Chevening Scholarships (for PhD study at King's College London)

title: King's College London Health and Social Care Research PhD Studentships (NIHR-related)

title: LSE Law School PhD Studentship

title: Wellcome Trust Doctoral Studentship in Global Health and Conflict
summary: Wellcome Trust doctoral funding supports PhD research in global health, including health in conflict and humanitarian settings, at UK host institutions advertised via FindAPhD. Awards generally cover full fees, stipend, and research costs. Specific projects and deadlines are listed per host university.

title: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships (Humanitarian and Development Studies)
summary: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships fund doctoral study at UK universities for candidates from low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries, including in humanitarian, disaster management, and global health fields. The scheme covers tuition, stipend, and travel. Relevant opportunities are listed on FindAPhD by participating institutions.

title: Leverhulme Trust Doctoral Scholarship in International Humanitarian Law and Conflict
summary: Leverhulme Trust doctoral scholarships support PhD research across disciplines including international humanitarian law and conflict studies at UK host universities. Funding typically covers fees, stipend, and research expenses. Opportunities are advertised through FindAPhD by host institutions.

title: AHRC-funded PhD Studentship in Humanitarian and Disaster Studies
summary: Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC) studentships via UK doctoral training partnerships fund PhD research relevant to humanitarian studies, disaster management, and migration. Awards include fees, stipend, and training support. Listings appear on FindAPhD through participating universities.

Applicants must be nominated by a French host institution.

title: French Government Scholarship (BGF) - Doctoral Mobility

summary: The Fogarty Global Health Fellows and Scholars Program supports mentored clinical research training for pre- and postdoctoral trainees at low- and middle-income country sites. title: Fogarty HIV Research Training Program (D43)
summary: The Fogarty HIV Research Training Program funds institutional research training grants that support doctoral and postdoctoral trainees in low- and middle-income countries. Trainees receive mentored research training in HIV-related science, often in settings affected by conflict and displacement.

title: Fogarty International Research Training Grants (D71)
summary: Fogarty's international research training grants support doctoral and postdoctoral research training at institutions in low- and middle-income countries. These grants build research capacity in global health topics that can include humanitarian crises, migration, and disaster response.

title: Aga Khan University PhD in Health Policy and Management
summary: This doctoral programme at AKU's Medical College trains researchers in health policy, management, and systems strengthening, with relevance to humanitarian and fragile settings. title: Aga Khan University Institute for Human Development PhD Fellowships
summary: The Institute for Human Development at AKU supports doctoral research on human development, early childhood, and social determinants of health, including work relevant to displacement and vulnerable populations. Fellowships and research funding are offered to doctoral candidates affiliated with the Institute.

title: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme (PhD)
summary: The Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme provides scholarships and loans to outstanding students from developing countries for postgraduate and doctoral study, including fields such as health, humanitarian affairs, and development. Awards are granted on a competitive basis and cover tuition and living costs for study at selected institutions.

title: Aga Khan University PhD in Nursing Sciences
summary: AKU's School of Nursing and Midwifery offers a PhD in Nursing Sciences focused on clinical practice, health systems, and community health relevant to humanitarian and resource-limited contexts. It covers tuition, living stipend, airfare, Korean language training, and settlement allowance. Applicants may pursue PhD research in fields such as global health, international development, and public policy at participating Korean universities.

title: ICCR Commonwealth Scholarship / Fellowship (Doctoral Research in India)

key_figures.research_focus: Research on international humanitarian law and humanitarian action, including legal frameworks governing armed conflict and protection of civilians.

title: Uppsala University Department of Women's and Children's Health PhD Position in Global Health
summary: The Department of Women's and Children's Health at Uppsala University offers doctoral positions in global health, including research on health in conflict and humanitarian settings. These are fully funded salaried positions, often linked to international collaborations and projects on maternal and child health in low-resource and crisis-affected contexts.

key_figures.name: Peter Allebeck
key_figures.title: Professor of Social Medicine
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on social epidemiology, global health, and the health consequences of conflict and displacement, including studies on mental health among refugee populations.

key_figures.name: Anna Mia Ekström
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health with emphasis on HIV, sexual and reproductive health, and health systems in low-resource and conflict-affected settings.

key_figures.name: Hans Rosling
key_figures.title: Professor of International Health (deceased 2017)
key_figures.research_focus: Pioneered global health research and data visualization, focusing on the links between economic development, health, and conflict in low-income countries.

title: Swedish Institute (SI) Scholarships for Global Professionals
summary: The Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals (SISGP) fund master's-level studies rather than PhDs, but are sometimes confused with doctoral funding; they support students from certain countries to study at Swedish universities including Uppsala. For doctoral studies, applicants should instead look to university-advertised doktorandtjänster or research council grants.

key_figures.name: Hans Rosling
key_figures.title: Professor of International Health (deceased 2017)
key_figures.research_focus: Global health, epidemiology, and socioeconomic development; founded Gapminder to promote fact-based worldview on global health and poverty trends.

key_figures.name: Peter Wallensteen
key_figures.title: Senior Professor of Peace and Conflict Research
key_figures.research_focus: Peace and conflict research, armed conflict, mediation, and humanitarian consequences of war; former Dag Hammarskjöld Professor at Uppsala University.

key_figures.name: Ashok Swain
key_figures.title: Professor of Peace and Conflict Research
key_figures.research_focus: Forced migration, climate change and conflict, water sharing, and global governance; director of the Research School on International Water Cooperation at Uppsala University.

title: University of Milan PhD Programme in Legal Studies - Doctoral Fellowship
summary: The PhD in Legal Studies at the University of Milan includes funded positions for research in international law, human rights, and humanitarian law. Selected candidates receive a scholarship covering living costs and research activities.

key_figures.name: Chiara Ragni
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the protection of migrants and refugees, including the law of armed conflict and international criminal justice.

key_figures.name: Marco Pedrazzi
key_figures.title: Full Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on public international law, international humanitarian law, human rights, and international criminal law, with attention to armed conflicts and individual responsibility.

key_figures.name: Maurizio Arcari
key_figures.title: Full Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international law, human rights, refugee protection, and the law of international organizations, including issues related to forced migration and asylum.

title: PhD in Social and Political Sciences - Doctoral Studentship (University of Milan)
summary: This doctoral programme at the University of Milan offers funded studentships for research on migration, social policy, and crisis response. The scholarship includes a stipend, tuition waiver, and support for research stays abroad.

title: PhD Programme in Political Science and International Relations (Dottorato in Scienze Politiche)
summary: Doctoral programme at the University of Pisa focused on political science, international relations, and related fields such as migration and conflict studies. Funded PhD positions are awarded through competitive selection with a stipend and research allowance. Suitable for candidates researching humanitarian and forced migration topics.

key_figures.name: Emanuele Sommario
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the protection of persons in armed conflict and disaster settings. He has published extensively on humanitarian access, forced migration, and the legal frameworks governing international responses to crises.

key_figures.name: Andrea de Guttry
key_figures.title: Full Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international humanitarian law, human rights, peacekeeping, and the legal dimensions of forced migration and refugee protection. He has led major research projects on humanitarian crises, international security, and the role of international organizations.

key_figures.name: Francesca Capone
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international human rights law, humanitarian law, and the protection of vulnerable groups including refugees and internally displaced persons. Her work addresses forced migration, human trafficking, and international legal responses to displacement.

title: Italian Government Scholarship for International Students (MAECI)
summary: Scholarships offered by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation (MAECI) to international students, including for PhD study at Italian universities such as the University of Pisa. Covers tuition, a monthly allowance, and health insurance. Applicants apply through the Study in Italy portal.

title: PhD Programme in Earth Sciences / Environmental Sciences (Dottorato in Scienze della Terra)
summary: Doctoral programme at the University of Pisa covering earth sciences, environmental risk, and geohazards relevant to disaster management. Funded PhD positions include a stipend and research support. Open to international candidates via competitive admission.

key_figures.name: Nicola Casagli
key_figures.title: Full Professor of Engineering Geology
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on landslide monitoring and early warning systems, geohazard assessment, and the application of remote sensing (InSAR, GB-InSAR) for slope stability and disaster risk reduction.

key_figures.name: Veronica Tofani
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of Engineering Geology
key_figures.research_focus: Works on landslide susceptibility and hazard mapping, geohazard assessment using remote sensing and GIS, and integrated approaches for environmental risk management.

key_figures.name: Filippo Catani
key_figures.title: Full Professor of Geomorphology and Geohazards
key_figures.research_focus: Investigates landslide hazard and risk modelling, geomorphological processes, and the use of statistical and machine learning methods for disaster risk assessment.

title: Leiden University Medical Center (LUMC) PhD Position
summary: LUMC, the medical faculty of Leiden University, offers salaried PhD positions in biomedical and public/global health research, including topics related to health in humanitarian and conflict settings. Positions are advertised on an ongoing basis and are fully funded as employment contracts.

key_figures.name: Maria Yazdanbakhsh
key_figures.title: Professor of Cellular Immunology of Parasitic Infections
key_figures.research_focus: Her research focuses on immune responses to parasitic infections and how these shape vaccine responses and disease outcomes in low- and middle-income countries, with strong ties to global health immunology.

key_figures.name: Jan Aart Scholte
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Transformations and Governance
key_figures.research_focus: He studies global governance, civil society, and institutional responses to transnational crises, including health emergencies and conflict-related governance challenges.

key_figures.name: Dennis Broeders
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Security and Technology
key_figures.research_focus: His work examines global security governance, cybersecurity, and the role of technology in conflict and crisis management, including implications for disaster and health emergency response.

title: Leiden University Fund (LUF) / Leiden University Scholarships for PhD Candidates
summary: Leiden University offers various scholarship schemes (including LUF and faculty-specific funds) that can support PhD candidates, though most full PhD funding comes through salaried employment. These scholarships may cover partial costs such as travel, fieldwork, or living expenses for doctoral research.

key_figures.name: Thea Hilhorst
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Research on humanitarian aid, conflict, displacement, and the everyday politics of humanitarian governance. She studies how humanitarian crises and forced migration are addressed in fragile settings.

key_figures.name: Marleen Dekker
key_figures.title: Professor of African Studies and Director of the African Studies Centre Leiden
key_figures.research_focus: Research on global health, poverty, social protection, and development in Africa, with attention to migration and health vulnerabilities. She works on inclusive development and access to health services.

key_figures.name: Anouk Rigterink
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on forced migration, conflict, and humanitarian outcomes, including the effects of displacement on health and well-being. Her work combines quantitative methods with field research in conflict-affected regions.

title: NWO PhD in the Humanities (Open Competition / Vici-Veni-linked positions)
summary: NWO (Dutch Research Council) funds PhD positions embedded in research projects at Utrecht University, including in the humanities and social sciences. Projects linked to Vici, Vidi, and Veni grants at Utrecht University frequently include fully-funded doctoral positions on migration, humanitarianism, and international law.

key_figures.name: Joris van Wijk
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research focuses on international crimes, terrorism, and forced migration, including the legal position of refugees and asylum seekers. He examines how international humanitarian law and criminal law intersect with migration governance.

key_figures.name: Marjolein van den Brink
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international humanitarian law, human rights, and gender, with attention to armed conflict and displacement. Her research addresses legal protection gaps for forced migrants and conflict-affected populations.

key_figures.name: Conny Rijken
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Specializes in human trafficking, forced migration, and international law. Her work examines legal frameworks protecting migrants in vulnerable situations, including victims of trafficking and forced displacement.

title: Utrecht University Centre for Global Challenges PhD Affiliates
summary: The Centre for Global Challenges at Utrecht University brings together researchers working on conflict, human rights, migration, and global health, and hosts or affiliates PhD candidates on these themes. Funding arrangements vary by project, often combining university employment with external grants.

key_figures.name: Joris Schapendonk
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on migration trajectories, forced migration, and the everyday politics of mobility, with a focus on African migration to Europe.

key_figures.name: Ilse van Liempt
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Works on forced migration, refugee reception, and the governance of migration in urban contexts, with attention to humanitarian responses.

key_figures.name: Charles Agyemang
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Global health researcher focusing on ethnic inequalities in health, migration and health, and cardiovascular disease prevention among migrant populations.

title: Utrecht University Descartes Centre / Humanities PhD Positions
summary: The Descartes Centre for the History and Philosophy of the Sciences and the Humanities at Utrecht University hosts fully-funded PhD candidates, some of whom work on humanitarian history, international law, and migration. Positions are advertised via the university's vacancy system and are open to international applicants.

key_figures.name: Jeroen Doomernik
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on migration governance, asylum and refugee policies, and the politics of forced migration in Europe. He has published extensively on irregular migration, migrant smuggling, and the reception of asylum seekers.

key_figures.name: Barbara Oomen
key_figures.title: Professor of Sociology of Human Rights
key_figures.research_focus: Works on the local and international dimensions of human rights, including the role of cities in protecting refugees and migrants. Her research connects international human rights law with humanitarian practice and forced migration governance.

key_figures.name: Cedric Ryngaert
key_figures.title: Professor of Public International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international humanitarian law, international criminal law, and the law of armed conflict, including issues of jurisdiction and accountability. His work also touches on the legal frameworks governing forced migration in conflict settings.

title: UvA PhD Positions (Doctoral Employment) via Academic Transfer
summary: The University of Amsterdam advertises most of its fully-funded PhD vacancies as salaried four-year employment contracts through the national Academic Transfer portal. Positions relevant to humanitarian studies, forced migration, conflict health, and international law appear regularly across UvA faculties. Each vacancy specifies its own project, supervisor, and application deadline.

key_figures.name: Rebecca Bryant
key_figures.title: Professor of Cultural Anthropology
key_figures.research_focus: Research on forced migration, displacement, and humanitarianism, with a focus on the politics of belonging and sovereignty in the Eastern Mediterranean. She has led major projects on displacement and humanitarian governance.

key_figures.name: Darshan Vigneswaran
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of Political Science
key_figures.research_focus: Research on migration governance, forced migration, and the politics of mobility, particularly in Africa and the Global South. He directs the Migration and Development research group.

key_figures.name: Saskia Bonjour
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of Political Science
key_figures.research_focus: Research on migration politics, refugee policies, and the governance of forced migration in Europe. She studies how states and institutions respond to displacement and humanitarian crises.

title: VU Amsterdam Migration and Diversity PhD Positions (Faculty of Social Sciences)
summary: VU Amsterdam's Faculty of Social Sciences, including groups researching migration, diversity, and conflict, regularly advertises fully-funded salaried PhD positions relevant to forced migration and humanitarian themes. These are four-year employee contracts with salary and benefits. Openings are listed on the VU working-at portal.

key_figures.name: Jeroen Doomernik
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Research on migration governance, asylum and refugee policies, and the politics of forced migration in Europe. Focuses on how states and institutions manage migration and humanitarian protection.

key_figures.name: Halleh Ghorashi
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Works on forced migration, refugee integration, and humanitarianism, with attention to diasporic identity, belonging, and the politics of inclusion and exclusion.

key_figures.name: Dorothea Hilhorst
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Leading scholar in humanitarian studies and disaster management, researching humanitarian aid, crisis governance, and the everyday politics of disaster response.

title: Netherlands Fellowship Programme (NFP) – PhD at Wageningen University
summary: The Netherlands Fellowship Programme (administered by Nuffic) provides full scholarships for professionals from selected countries to pursue PhD studies in the Netherlands, including at Wageningen University. It covers tuition, living costs, and travel. Eligible fields include development studies, health, and disaster-related research.

key_figures.name: Thea Hilhorst
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies

key_figures.name: Ruerd Ruben

key_figures.name: Jeroen Warner

title: TU Delft Graduate School Doctoral Scholarship / PhD Funding
summary: TU Delft's Graduate School provides structured doctoral training and funding for PhD candidates, who are typically employed under Dutch collective labour agreement terms with salary and benefits. Research themes include safety, security, and resilience relevant to disaster management and humanitarian engineering.

title: TU Delft | Global Initiative PhD Funding / Delft Global Fellowship
summary: The TU Delft Global Initiative supports research and doctoral projects focused on global challenges including health, water, and humanitarian technology in low- and middle-income countries. It provides funding and co-supervision for PhD candidates working on development-oriented topics.

key_figures.name: Thea Hilhorst
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Research on humanitarian aid, disaster response, and the politics of humanitarianism, with a focus on crisis-affected regions and the intersection of humanitarian action with development and peacebuilding.

key_figures.name: Bartel Van de Walle

key_figures.name: Tina Comes

title: Erasmus Initiative Dynamics of Inclusive Prosperity PhD Position
summary: Erasmus University Rotterdam's strategic initiatives, such as Dynamics of Inclusive Prosperity, periodically fund PhD positions addressing societal challenges. key_figures.name: Thea Hilhorst
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Her research focuses on humanitarian aid, conflict, disasters, and forced migration, with attention to the everyday politics of humanitarian governance and crisis response.

key_figures.name: Peter Heintze
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor
key_figures.research_focus: His work examines global health governance, humanitarian action, and the politics of health in crisis-affected and forced migration settings.

key_figures.name: Zeynep Kasli
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor
key_figures.research_focus: She researches forced migration, humanitarianism, and displacement governance, with a focus on refugee protection and the politics of aid in the Middle East and Europe.

title: Erasmus MC PhD Position in Global Health / Humanitarian Health
summary: Erasmus MC, the medical centre of Erasmus University Rotterdam, regularly advertises fully-funded PhD positions in global and humanitarian health. These salaried positions are linked to specific research projects and supervisors. Vacancies are posted on the Erasmus MC and EUR job portals.

key_figures.name: Theodora (Doris) A. M. W. van der Kwaak
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on sexual and reproductive health and rights in fragile settings, conflict-affected areas, and low-resource countries, with attention to health systems and community-based approaches.

key_figures.name: Ivan Speek
key_figures.title: Researcher
key_figures.research_focus: Works on humanitarian action, disaster management, and conflict-related health and protection issues, with a focus on aid effectiveness and local humanitarian response.

key_figures.name: Ruerd Ruben
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Conducts research on food security, rural development, and the resilience of livelihoods in conflict-affected and disaster-prone regions, linking global health and development outcomes.

title: PhD Position in International Law / International Humanitarian Law (University of Groningen Faculty of Law)
summary: The Faculty of Law at the University of Groningen periodically advertises fully-funded PhD positions in international law, including international humanitarian law and human rights. These salaried positions run for four years and include supervision, training, and conference funding. Openings appear on the university vacancy page.

key_figures.name: Marcel Brus
key_figures.title: Professor Emeritus of Public International Law

key_figures.name: Cedric Ryngaert
key_figures.title: Professor of Public International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Public international law, jurisdiction and immunities, international human rights law, and business and human rights.

key_figures.name: Antenor Hallo de Wolf
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Law

title: Ubbo Emmius Fund / Groningen University Fund PhD Support
summary: The Ubbo Emmius Fund and the Groningen University Fund provide supplementary financial support for PhD research and scholarships at the University of Groningen. These funds can co-finance doctoral projects, including those in global health, migration, and humanitarian themes. Support is typically awarded through internal university procedures.

key_figures.name: Jelle Stekelenburg
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health

key_figures.name: Ajay Bailey
key_figures.title: Professor of Social Demography
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health, migration, ageing, and urban health using interdisciplinary social science approaches, including humanitarian and equity perspectives.

key_figures.name: Marleen Dekker

title: UQ-Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) Postgraduate Scholarship
summary: The CSIRO Postgraduate Scholarship supports PhD students at UQ undertaking research aligned with CSIRO's priority areas, including health, environment, and disaster resilience. It provides a stipend and operating funds, and is co-funded by CSIRO and the university.

key_figures.name: Brian Head
key_figures.title: Professor

key_figures.name: Paul Henman
key_figures.title: Associate Professor

key_figures.name: Claire Wyatt-Smith
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on assessment, health professions education, and public health workforce development, including preparedness for complex health challenges.

title: Australian Awards Scholarship (Australia Awards) at UQ
summary: Australia Awards Scholarships are funded by the Australian Government's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade and are available to students from developing countries to undertake postgraduate study, including PhDs, at Australian universities such as UQ. They cover tuition, living expenses, and travel, and support fields such as global health, humanitarian studies, and disaster management.

key_figures.name: Professor Peter Hill
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health

key_figures.name: Professor Rob Cramb

key_figures.name: Dr. Lisa Schubert

title: Research School of Population Health HDR Scholarships
summary: The ANU Research School of Population Health offers HDR scholarships for PhD candidates researching population health, including global health, conflict health, and disaster management. Scholarships typically include a stipend and fee remission.

key_figures.name: Kamalini Lokuge
key_figures.title: Associate Professor

key_figures.name: Paul Kelly
key_figures.title: Professor

key_figures.name: Ryutaro Murotani
key_figures.title: Research Fellow

title: ANU College of Asia and the Pacific HDR Scholarships
summary: The ANU College of Asia and the Pacific offers HDR scholarships for PhD research on the Asia-Pacific region, including forced migration, humanitarian studies, and disaster management. Awards typically include stipend and fee remission.

key_figures.name: Bina D'Costa

key_figures.name: Alan Gamlen

key_figures.name: Helen James

title: ANU Fenner School of Environment and Society HDR Scholarships
summary: The ANU Fenner School of Environment and Society offers HDR scholarships for PhD research in environmental and societal fields, including disaster management and global health. Scholarships generally include stipend and fee remission.

key_figures.name: Peter Grabosky

title: Monash University Postgraduate Publications Award

key_figures.name: Michael J. Selgelid

title: Monash Silver Jubilee Postgraduate Scholarship

summary: Commonwealth Scholarships enable students from Commonwealth countries to pursue PhD study in New Zealand, including at Victoria University of Wellington. Funding typically covers tuition, stipend, and travel, and can support research in global health, law, and humanitarian studies.
