key_figures.research_focus: Research on international law, international humanitarian law, and human rights, including the legal frameworks governing armed conflict and the protection of vulnerable populations.

title: New Zealand Government Scholarship (New Zealand Scholarships)
summary: New Zealand Government Scholarships fund full tuition, living costs, and travel for eligible international students from developing countries to pursue postgraduate and PhD study at New Zealand universities including the University of Canterbury. Relevant fields include development, health, and disaster resilience.

title: HCRI PhD Studentships (Humanitarian and Conflict Response Institute)
summary: The Humanitarian and Conflict Response Institute (HCRI) at the University of Manchester offers PhD studentships and funded doctoral opportunities in humanitarian studies, conflict response, disaster management, and related fields. Funding typically covers tuition fees and a stipend, often linked to specific research projects or external grants.

key_figures.name: Rony Brauman
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on humanitarian action, medical ethics in conflict settings, and the politics of humanitarian intervention. Has written extensively on the dilemmas of humanitarian aid in war zones and disasters.

key_figures.name: Peter Walker
key_figures.title: Professor of Disaster Management
key_figures.research_focus: Researches disaster risk reduction, humanitarian response, and the intersection of climate change and conflict. Has led major studies on resilience and disaster management in fragile states.

key_figures.name: Bayard Roberts
key_figures.title: Professor of Health Systems and Policy
key_figures.research_focus: Investigates health systems in conflict-affected settings, mental health in humanitarian crises, and the delivery of health services during disasters. Leads research on conflict and health at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, with collaborations at Manchester.

title: King's College London Centre for Doctoral Training / London Interdisciplinary Doctoral Programme (LIDo) Studentship
summary: LIDo is a BBSRC-funded doctoral training partnership hosted partly at King's College London, offering fully-funded PhD studentships with stipend and fees. Projects can span health, bioscience, and interdisciplinary areas relevant to global and public health.

key_figures.name: Richard Sullivan
key_figures.title: Professor of Cancer and Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on global health systems, health in conflict and humanitarian settings, and the delivery of health services in crisis-affected populations.

key_figures.name: Preeti Patel
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the intersection of global health, conflict, and humanitarian response, with a focus on health systems in fragile and conflict-affected states.

key_figures.name: Rebecca Grais
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health emergencies, disaster response, and the epidemiology of populations affected by conflict and humanitarian crises.

title: King's College London & Wellcome Trust Doctoral Studentship
summary: Wellcome Trust funds doctoral studentships and programmes that can be hosted at King's College London, covering fees, stipend, and research costs. These support health-related research including global health, mental health in conflict, and humanitarian health topics.

key_figures.name: Richard Sullivan
key_figures.title: Professor of Cancer and Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on global health systems, health in conflict-affected settings, and the interface between humanitarian crises and cancer care. Directs the Institute of Cancer Policy and works extensively on health security and conflict health.

key_figures.name: Preeti Patel
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the intersection of global health, conflict, and humanitarian response, with a focus on health systems in fragile and conflict-affected states and the politics of humanitarian aid.

key_figures.name: Gemma Bowsher
key_figures.title: Research Fellow in Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Examines global health security, humanitarian health interventions, and the health impacts of conflict and displacement, with work on military-civilian health engagement and humanitarian policy.

title: King's College London & Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) Studentship (via UBEL DTP)
summary: The UBEL Doctoral Training Partnership, funded by the ESRC, offers fully-funded PhD studentships at King's College London in social science disciplines. These can support research on forced migration, humanitarian studies, and international law depending on the department and supervisor.

key_figures.name: Dr. Nicola Perugini
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer in International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international humanitarian law, the politics of human rights, and the legal and spatial dimensions of forced displacement and occupation.

key_figures.name: Professor Guglielmo Verdirame
key_figures.title: Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international humanitarian law, human rights law, and the legal frameworks governing refugees, migration, and armed conflict.

key_figures.name: Dr. Ruben Andersson
key_figures.title: Associate Professor in Anthropology
key_figures.research_focus: Studies forced migration, borders, and humanitarian responses, with ethnographic work on migration control and humanitarian interventions in West Africa and the Mediterranean.

title: King's College London & Medical Research Council (MRC) Doctoral Training Partnership Studentship
summary: The MRC Doctoral Training Partnership at King's College London provides fully-funded PhD studentships covering fees, stipend, and training. Research areas include global health, epidemiology, and health in conflict and disaster settings.

key_figures.name: Richard Sullivan
key_figures.title: Professor of Cancer and Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on global health systems, health in conflict and humanitarian settings, and the interface between health, security, and development. His work includes cancer care in low- and middle-income countries and health system resilience in crises.

key_figures.name: Preeti Patel
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health and Conflict
key_figures.research_focus: Researches the politics of global health in conflict-affected settings, health system strengthening in fragile states, and humanitarian health governance. Her work addresses conflict, displacement, and access to health services.

key_figures.name: Virginia Murray
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Disaster Risk Reduction
key_figures.research_focus: Works on disaster risk reduction, emergency preparedness, and public health aspects of disasters and climate-related hazards. She has contributed to international frameworks on disaster risk management and health emergency preparedness.

title: Chevening Scholarship (for PhD study at King's College London)
summary: Chevening is the UK government's international scholarship programme, funding outstanding emerging leaders from around the world to pursue a master's or PhD at UK universities including King's College London. It covers tuition, living costs, and travel, and is open to fields such as humanitarian studies, global health, and forced migration.

key_figures.name: Sara E. Davies
key_figures.title: Professor of Global Health Governance
key_figures.research_focus: Research on global health governance, health security, and the politics of pandemic preparedness, with attention to how international institutions respond to health emergencies and displacement.

key_figures.name: Simon Rushton
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer in International Politics
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health politics, health security, and the political determinants of health, including responses to epidemics and the governance of health in conflict-affected and displaced populations.

key_figures.name: Jenny Edkins
key_figures.title: Professor of Politics
key_figures.research_focus: Research on humanitarianism, forced migration, and the politics of memory and trauma, with critical work on humanitarian intervention and the experiences of displaced people.

title: LSE Middle East Centre / LSE IDEAS Conflict and Migration Doctoral Funding
summary: LSE research centres such as the Middle East Centre and LSE IDEAS periodically offer doctoral funding or bursaries for research on conflict, migration and humanitarian issues. These awards may be partial and are usually advertised alongside specific research projects or themes.

key_figures.name: Bayard Roberts
key_figures.title: Professor of Health Policy and Systems
key_figures.research_focus: Research on health systems and mental health in conflict-affected and forced migration settings, including humanitarian crises and displacement.

key_figures.name: Mazeda Hossain
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of Social and Health Inequalities
key_figures.research_focus: Research on violence, health, and forced migration, including humanitarian settings and conflict-affected populations.

key_figures.name: Chaloka Beyani
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Law
key_figures.research_focus: Research on international humanitarian law, forced displacement, and the protection of refugees and internally displaced persons.

title: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships (hosted at LSE)
summary: Commonwealth PhD Scholarships, funded by the UK government and tenable at UK universities including LSE, provide full funding for doctoral study to candidates from low and middle income Commonwealth countries. They cover tuition fees, stipend and travel, and support research in development-related fields such as health, migration and humanitarian studies.

key_figures.name: Sara E. Davies
key_figures.title: Professor of International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Research on global health governance, health security, and the politics of pandemic preparedness, with attention to how international institutions respond to health emergencies.

key_figures.name: Clare Wenham
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of Global Health Policy
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health policy, pandemic preparedness, and the politics of health emergencies, including the intersection of health and foreign policy.

key_figures.name: Kirsten Ainley
key_figures.title: Associate Professor of International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Research on international criminal justice, human rights, and humanitarian intervention, with broader interests in ethics and international politics.

title: Wellcome Trust Doctoral Studentship in Global Health (FindAPhD-listed)
summary: FindAPhD aggregates fully-funded PhD studentships advertised by UK and international universities, including Wellcome Trust-funded doctoral programmes in global health and humanitarian health. These studentships typically cover tuition, stipend, and research costs for three to four years. Applicants apply through the host university, with FindAPhD serving as the listing platform.

title: ESRC-funded PhD Studentship in Forced Migration (FindAPhD-listed)
summary: FindAPhD lists Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) doctoral studentships hosted at UK universities through Doctoral Training Partnerships, including projects on forced migration, refugee studies, and humanitarian response. Funding usually includes fees, a maintenance stipend, and a research training support grant. Applications are made to the specific host university.

title: Doctoral Fellowship in International Humanitarian Law (FindAPhD-listed)
summary: FindAPhD advertises PhD fellowships at law schools and research centres working on international humanitarian law, armed conflict, and humanitarian protection. These are typically fully-funded three-year doctoral positions combining stipend, tuition, and research expenses. Candidates apply directly to the advertising institution.

title: Fully-Funded PhD Studentship in Disaster Management and Resilience (FindAPhD-listed)
summary: FindAPhD hosts listings for fully-funded doctoral studentships in disaster risk reduction, resilience, and humanitarian logistics, often funded by research councils or university schemes. Awards generally cover tuition fees, a tax-free stipend, and fieldwork or training costs. Applicants apply through the host department.

title: Commonwealth PhD Scholarship (FindAPhD-listed)
summary: FindAPhD lists Commonwealth PhD Scholarships for candidates from low- and middle-income Commonwealth countries, applicable to development-related fields including global health, forced migration, and humanitarian studies at UK universities. The scheme covers tuition, stipend, airfare, and thesis grant. Applications are submitted through the Commonwealth Scholarship Commission and host university.

title: DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme (Public Policy and Good Governance) – related doctoral pathways
summary: The Helmut-Schmidt-Programme funds future leaders from developing and emerging countries in public policy, governance, and law-related master's and doctoral-linked study at German institutions. It supports study relevant to humanitarian governance, international law, and migration policy, though applicants should confirm doctoral eligibility with the specific host programme.

title: DAAD Doctoral Scholarships for Developing and Emerging Countries (Research Grants – Short-Term and Long-Term)
summary: DAAD offers long-term and short-term doctoral research grants for candidates from developing and emerging countries to pursue PhD research in Germany. Funding includes monthly stipend, insurance, and travel, and is applicable to development-relevant fields such as global health, disaster management, and forced migration.

title: Eiffel Excellence Scholarship Program – Doctorate
summary: The Eiffel Excellence Scholarship Program, managed by Campus France, funds doctoral students (among master's and PhD levels) for up to 12 months of PhD study in France. It provides a monthly stipend, travel costs, and insurance for international candidates in priority fields including health, law, and social sciences.

title: Campus France – French Government Scholarships (Bourses du Gouvernement Français)
summary: Campus France coordinates French Government Scholarships (BGF) offered through French embassies worldwide, which can fund doctoral studies in France across disciplines including public health, law, and social sciences. Awards typically cover tuition, monthly living allowance, and travel, with eligibility and deadlines set by each embassy.

title: Campus France – Doctorate in France (Doctorat) funding guidance and CIFRE/doctoral contracts
summary: Campus France's doctoral portal explains fully-funded PhD routes in France, including doctoral contracts (contrats doctoraux) funded by universities and research bodies, and CIFRE industrial agreements. These provide salaried PhD positions open to international candidates in fields such as public health, law, and social sciences.

title: Campus France – Charpak PhD Scholarship (Charpak Doctoral Fellowship)
summary: The Charpak Scholarship, administered by Campus France India, includes a doctoral research fellowship track supporting Indian PhD students for research stays in France. It offers a monthly stipend and support for research mobility in fields including health and social sciences.

title: EDUFI Fellowship (Finnish National Agency for Education)
summary: The EDUFI Fellowship is a doctoral-level grant administered by the Finnish National Agency for Education for foreign doctoral students and researchers to carry out research at Finnish universities. It provides a monthly allowance for a fixed period and is open to applicants in any discipline, including global health, humanitarian studies, and forced migration research.

title: PhD Scholarship in Global Health (Department of Public Health)
summary: Doctoral positions at the Department of Public Health funded through the University of Copenhagen's PhD School, covering salary and research costs. Projects often address global health, health systems, and equity in low- and middle-income settings.

key_figures.name: Ib Christian Bygbjerg
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Research on global health, infectious and non-communicable diseases, and health in low- and middle-income settings, with emphasis on maternal and child health and diabetes in resource-poor contexts.

key_figures.name: Flemming Konradsen
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health, environmental and occupational health, and health systems in low-resource settings, including water, sanitation, and pesticide exposure.

key_figures.name: Dan Wolf Meyrowitsch
key_figures.title: Associate Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Research on global health, health equity, and social determinants of health, with work on infectious disease control and health systems in low-income countries.

title: PhD Fellowship at the Centre for Advanced Migration Studies (AMIS)
summary: Doctoral fellowships hosted at the Centre for Advanced Migration Studies, which researches migration, displacement, and refugee dynamics. Fellows receive salary and research funding through the Faculty of Humanities PhD programme.

key_figures.name: Anja Kublitz
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Anthropological research on forced migration, refugee families, and the everyday lives of displaced people, with fieldwork among Palestinian refugees and in Denmark.

key_figures.name: Ninna Nyberg Sørensen
key_figures.title: Senior Researcher (emerita) / affiliated with University of Copenhagen
key_figures.research_focus: Migration and development, transnational migration, forced displacement, and gendered dimensions of migration, with extensive work on refugee and diaspora studies.

key_figures.name: Zachary Whyte
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Ethnographic research on asylum seekers, refugee reception, and the Danish asylum system, focusing on the lived experience of forced migration and bureaucratic processes.

title: PhD Scholarship at the Copenhagen Centre for Disaster Research (COPE)
summary: Doctoral research positions at COPE, which studies disaster risk, vulnerability, and humanitarian response. Funded PhD fellowships are offered through the Department of Public Health and Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences.

key_figures.name: Emmanuel Raju
key_figures.title: Professor (Associate Professor) of Disaster Risk Reduction, University of Copenhagen
key_figures.research_focus: Works on disaster risk reduction, humanitarian action, and climate adaptation, with emphasis on local knowledge, governance, and urban risk in the Global South.

key_figures.name: Peter Kjær Mackie Jensen
key_figures.title: Associate Professor, University of Copenhagen
key_figures.research_focus: Researches disaster management and humanitarian health, including water, sanitation, and disease risks in emergencies and refugee settings.

key_figures.name: Kristoffer Albris
key_figures.title: Associate Professor, University of Copenhagen
key_figures.research_focus: Studies disaster risk, crisis management, and humanitarian technology, including the use of digital data and drones in disaster response.

title: PhD Fellowship at the Centre for Military Studies / Conflict Research
summary: Doctoral fellowships at the Department of Political Science's Centre for Military Studies, covering armed conflict, security, and international law. Funded through the Faculty of Social Sciences PhD School.

key_figures.name: Erik Møse
key_figures.title: Professor Emeritus, Faculty of Law
key_figures.research_focus: International humanitarian law, international criminal law, and human rights, with experience as a judge at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia.

key_figures.name: Mikkel Jarle Christensen
key_figures.title: Professor, Faculty of Law
key_figures.research_focus: International criminal justice, international humanitarian law, and the sociology of international law, including the role of legal professionals in conflict and post-conflict settings.

key_figures.name: Anders Henriksen
key_figures.title: Associate Professor, Faculty of Law
key_figures.research_focus: International security law, the use of force, international humanitarian law, and legal aspects of cyber and hybrid threats.

title: University of Copenhagen PhD School General Scholarship
summary: The central PhD School at the University of Copenhagen advertises fully funded doctoral positions across faculties, including health, social sciences, and humanities. Positions relevant to humanitarian and global health research are regularly posted through this portal.

key_figures.name: Peter Kjær Mackie Jensen
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Works on global health, diarrheal disease, and water/sanitation in low-resource and humanitarian settings, including refugee contexts.

key_figures.name: Anja Olsen
key_figures.title: Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Researches global health epidemiology and nutrition, with work relevant to humanitarian and low-resource populations.

key_figures.name: Morten Sodemann
key_figures.title: Associate Professor, Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on global health, migration and health, and humanitarian medicine, including care for refugees and migrants.

title: Danish Council for Independent Research (DFF) Doctoral Fellowship hosted at UCPH
summary: The Danish Council for Independent Research funds individual doctoral and postdoctoral projects, many hosted at University of Copenhagen departments. Researchers in global health, conflict, and humanitarian fields can apply for project funding that supports PhD fellowships.

key_figures.name: Peter Vedsted
key_figures.title: Professor, Research Unit for General Practice, Department of Public Health
key_figures.research_focus: Health services research with focus on access to care, cancer diagnostics, and equity in health systems; involved in global health capacity building.

key_figures.name: Flemming Konradsen
key_figures.title: Professor, Department of Public Health; Director, Copenhagen School of Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global health with emphasis on environmental and occupational health, water and sanitation, and health in low-resource settings.

key_figures.name: Dan Wolf Meyrowitsch
key_figures.title: Associate Professor, Department of Public Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global health research on infectious disease epidemiology, health systems in low-income countries, and humanitarian health contexts.

title: Croatian Government Scholarship for Foreign Students (PhD studies)
summary: Bilateral scholarship scheme funded by the Croatian Ministry of Science and Education for foreign students, including doctoral candidates, to study at Croatian public universities. Covers tuition, monthly stipend, accommodation, and health insurance for the duration of study.

title: Erasmus+ / MSCA Doctoral Networks hosted at Croatian universities
summary: EU-funded Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions doctoral networks occasionally host PhD fellowships at Croatian institutions such as the University of Zagreb and University of Split. These provide full salary, mobility allowance, and research budget for international doctoral candidates.

title: University of Zagreb Doctoral Scholarships (through Ministry of Science and Education)
summary: Doctoral scholarships co-financed by the Croatian Ministry of Science and Education and Croatian universities to support PhD candidates enrolled at Croatian public universities. Funding typically covers partial stipend and research costs, with some programs taught in English.

title: Graduate Institute Doctoral Scholarship (PhD Funding)
summary: The Graduate Institute offers competitive doctoral scholarships covering tuition and a living stipend for admitted PhD students across its disciplines, including international relations, development, and related humanitarian and global health topics. Awards are typically granted at admission based on academic merit.

key_figures.name: Gilles Carbonnier
key_figures.title: Professor of Development Economics
key_figures.research_focus: Works on the political economy of development, humanitarian action, and the governance of international aid. His research examines humanitarianism, energy transitions, and the role of international organizations in development.

key_figures.name: Stephanie Hofmann
key_figures.title: Professor of International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Researches international security, international organizations, and the politics of multilateralism. Her work examines how institutions and alliances shape state behavior and global governance.

key_figures.name: Jean-Louis Arcand
key_figures.title: Professor of Development Economics
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on development economics, impact evaluation, and applied econometrics in low-income countries. His work addresses poverty, aid effectiveness, and household welfare in developing economies.

title: Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) Doctoral Fellowship / Doc.CH
summary: SNSF funding instruments such as Doc.CH and project-linked doctoral positions support PhD researchers at Swiss institutions, including the Graduate Institute. They cover salary and research costs for doctoral projects in the social sciences and humanities, including humanitarian and migration topics.

key_figures.name: Vinh-Kim Nguyen
key_figures.title: Professor of Anthropology and Global Health
key_figures.research_focus: Medical anthropologist and physician working on global health, humanitarianism, and the social dimensions of epidemics and HIV/AIDS in West Africa.

key_figures.title: Senior Researcher and Lecturer
key_figures.research_focus: Researches humanitarian action, humanitarian studies, and the politics of aid, with a focus on humanitarian governance and practice.

key_figures.name: Karl Blanchet
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Works on health systems in conflict and humanitarian settings, health in fragile states, and the effectiveness of humanitarian health interventions.

title: Graduate Institute Research Doctoral Studentships (Project-Funded PhD Positions)
summary: Doctoral positions attached to externally funded research projects at the Graduate Institute provide full funding (salary and tuition) for PhD candidates working on specific research themes, which can include humanitarian action, conflict, and global health. These are advertised as vacancies on the Institute's jobs and research pages.

key_figures.name: Vincent Bernard
key_figures.title: Senior Researcher and Lecturer in International Humanitarian Law
key_figures.research_focus: Works on international humanitarian law, the protection of persons in armed conflict, and the interplay between IHL and humanitarian practice. His research addresses legal and operational challenges in contemporary armed conflicts.

key_figures.name: Doris Schopper
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Researches humanitarian action, health in crises, and the ethics and effectiveness of humanitarian interventions. Her work spans conflict health, humanitarian studies, and public health in complex emergencies.

key_figures.name: Karl Blanchet
key_figures.title: Professor of Humanitarian Studies
key_figures.research_focus: Focuses on health systems in conflict and humanitarian settings, humanitarian studies, and evidence-based humanitarian response. His research examines health service delivery and resilience in fragile and conflict-affected states.

title: Qatar Foundation Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Doctoral Student Research Award
summary: Qatar Foundation's RDI pillar funds research awards and student research grants, including support for doctoral students conducting research aligned with QF's priority areas such as health and social development. Awards are competitive and typically cover research costs and stipends rather than full tuition.

title: Qatar National Research Fund (QNRF) Graduate Student Research Award (GSRA)
summary: QNRF, a member of Qatar Foundation, runs the Graduate Student Research Award (GSRA) supporting master's and doctoral students at Qatari institutions to conduct research within QNRF-funded projects. It provides stipends and research support for graduate research in priority areas including health and social sciences.

title: Hamad Bin Khalifa University (HBKU) PhD Scholarships
summary: HBKU, a Qatar Foundation member university, offers competitive PhD scholarships covering tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation, and travel for admitted doctoral students across its colleges, including the College of Public Policy and College of Health and Life Sciences. Research themes can touch on migration, public policy, and health.

title: Qatar University PhD Scholarship (Qatar Foundation-affiliated research collaboration)
summary: Qatar University offers fully-funded PhD scholarships (tuition, stipend, housing) for doctoral candidates, with research often conducted in collaboration with Qatar Foundation entities such as QNRF and Hamad Bin Khalifa University. Relevant for health, policy, and disaster-related research.

title: Fogarty Global Health Fellowship (FGHF) - Doctoral Trainee Track
summary: The Fogarty Global Health Fellowship supports predoctoral and postdoctoral trainees from the U.S. and low- and middle-income countries to conduct mentored global health research abroad for 10-12 months. Doctoral trainees in health-related fields, including global health and humanitarian health research, receive stipend, travel, and research support.

title: Fogarty International Clinical Research Scholars and Fellows Program (FICRS-F)
summary: This Fogarty program provides mentored clinical research training for doctoral-level health science students and postdoctoral fellows at partner sites in low- and middle-income countries. It supports a year of research abroad relevant to global health, including settings affected by conflict and displacement.

title: Fogarty HIV Research Training Program (HIVRT) - Doctoral Training Grants
summary: The Fogarty HIV Research Training Program funds institutional training grants that support doctoral and postdoctoral trainees in LMIC institutions to build HIV-related research capacity. Trainees receive stipends and research support, with relevance to global health in humanitarian and displacement-affected settings.

title: Aga Khan University PhD Fellowship in Health Sciences
summary: Aga Khan University offers doctoral fellowships supporting PhD candidates in health sciences, including public health and global health research relevant to low-resource and conflict-affected settings. Fellowships typically cover tuition, stipend, and research costs for the duration of the doctoral program.

key_figures.name: Zulfiqar A. Bhutta
key_figures.title: Professor and Chair, Department of Paediatrics; Director, Centre of Excellence in Women and Child Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global maternal, newborn, and child health, with work on nutrition, infectious disease, and health systems in low- and middle-income and conflict-affected settings.

key_figures.name: Sajjad Ali
key_figures.title: Assistant Professor, Community Health Sciences
key_figures.research_focus: Public health and health systems research, including primary health care and community-based interventions in Pakistan and the region.

key_figures.name: Asad Ali
key_figures.title: Professor and Chair, Department of Paediatrics and Child Health
key_figures.research_focus: Global child health, vaccine-preventable diseases, and infectious disease epidemiology in low-resource and conflict-affected populations.

title: Aga Khan University PhD Programme in Public Health (fully-funded studentship)
summary: The PhD in Public Health at Aga Khan University provides funded doctoral training with research opportunities in health systems, humanitarian health, and population health in South Asia and East Africa. Selected candidates receive tuition support and stipends while conducting field-based research.

title: Aga Khan University Institute for Human Development Doctoral Research Fellowship
summary: The Aga Khan University Institute for Human Development in East Africa supports doctoral research fellowships focused on human development, including migration, health, and social welfare in the region. Fellows conduct research aligned with the Institute's mission on improving quality of life in developing societies.

title: ICRC Doctoral Fellowship in Humanitarian Studies
summary: The ICRC supports doctoral research on humanitarian action, IHL, and protection of persons affected by armed conflict, often through partnerships with academic institutions. Fellowships typically cover stipend, research costs, and fieldwork support for PhD candidates whose work aligns with ICRC priorities.

title: ICRC Research Fellowship on Conflict and Health
summary: This fellowship supports doctoral-level research on health in armed conflict, including access to care, health systems under stress, and protection of medical personnel. It is typically hosted with partner universities and provides funding for research, travel, and dissemination.

title: ICRC Doctoral Fellowship on Forced Migration and Displacement
summary: Fellowship supporting PhD research on displacement caused by armed conflict, including legal protection, humanitarian response, and durable solutions. Awards typically include a stipend and research budget, with academic supervision through a partner institution.

title: ICRC Fellowship in International Humanitarian Law
summary: Doctoral fellowship for research on IHL doctrine, compliance, and contemporary challenges such as new technologies and asymmetric conflict. Funding supports dissertation research and engagement with ICRC legal experts and academic partners.

title: ICRC Doctoral Fellowship in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Response
summary: Fellowship for PhD candidates researching disaster preparedness, response coordination, and intersections between disasters and armed conflict. Provides stipend and research support, often in collaboration with academic centers specializing in humanitarian operations.

title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) - Graduate Program for Doctoral Degrees
summary: The Global Korea Scholarship (formerly Korean Government Scholarship Program, KGSP) funds international students for full doctoral degrees at Korean universities, covering tuition, airfare, monthly stipend, settlement allowance, and Korean language training. Applicants can pursue fields relevant to humanitarian studies, global health, and development at participating Korean graduate schools.

title: GKS Doctoral Program - Seoul National University (Graduate School of Public Health / International Studies)
summary: Through the GKS program, doctoral candidates can be hosted at Seoul National University's Graduate School of Public Health and Graduate School of International Studies, where research on global health, health policy, and international development is conducted. Funding includes full tuition, living stipend, and research support for the duration of the doctoral program.

title: GKS Doctoral Program - Yonsei University (Graduate School of International Studies / Institute for Global Health)
summary: Yonsei University participates in the GKS doctoral scholarship scheme, hosting international PhD students in its Graduate School of International Studies and global health research units. The scholarship covers tuition, stipend, airfare, and language training, supporting research on international cooperation, health, and humanitarian topics.

title: GKS Doctoral Program - Korea University (Graduate School of International Studies)
summary: Korea University's Graduate School of International Studies hosts GKS doctoral scholars pursuing research in international development, global governance, and related humanitarian fields. The fully-funded scholarship provides tuition, monthly allowance, airfare, and Korean language instruction.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship (CGS) – Bilateral Program
summary: The Bilateral Program is a full Chinese Government Scholarship administered by the China Scholarship Council (CSC) for international students pursuing doctoral degrees at Chinese universities. It typically covers tuition, accommodation, a monthly stipend, and medical insurance, and can support PhD research in public health, global health, and related social science fields at host universities.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship – Chinese University Program
summary: The Chinese University Program is a CSC-administered full scholarship through which designated Chinese universities recruit international PhD students. It generally funds tuition, living stipend, accommodation, and insurance, and is used by universities to support doctoral research across disciplines including public health, health policy, and social sciences relevant to humanitarian and global health studies.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship – Silk Road Program
summary: The Silk Road Program is a CSC full scholarship for international students from Belt and Road countries to pursue degree programs, including PhDs, at Chinese universities. It covers tuition, stipend, accommodation, and insurance, and can support doctoral study in health, policy, and development-related fields at participating institutions.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship – High Level Graduate Program
summary: The High Level Graduate Program is a CSC scholarship scheme supporting international students in master's and doctoral programs at selected Chinese universities. It provides full funding including tuition, living allowance, accommodation, and medical insurance, and is available for PhD research in health, law, and social science disciplines at host institutions.

title: Chinese Government Scholarship – University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS) Program
summary: This CSC-administered program funds international PhD students at the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences and affiliated institutes. It covers tuition, stipend, accommodation, and insurance, and supports doctoral research in health sciences, environmental and disaster-related sciences, and related fields.

title: University of Otago Health Sciences Career Development Award (PhD)
summary: The Health Sciences Career Development Award supports doctoral-level research within the Division of Health Sciences at Otago, covering stipend and research costs. It is aimed at researchers pursuing health-related doctoral projects, which can include global and conflict health themes.

key_figures.name: Philip Hill
key_figures.title: Professor of International Health
key_figures.research_focus: Leads research on global health, tuberculosis, and infectious disease epidemiology, with major work in low-resource settings including Southeast Asia and Africa. Directs the Centre for International Health at the University of Otago.

key_figures.name: Michael Baker
key_figures.title: Professor of Public Health
key_figures.research_focus: Public health physician researching infectious disease epidemiology, pandemic preparedness, and health system responses. Prominent voice on COVID-19 and public health policy in New Zealand.

key_figures.name: Robin Gauld
key_figures.title: Professor of Health Policy
key_figures.research_focus: Researches health policy, health systems, and global health governance, including comparative health system analysis and health sector reform. Dean of the Otago Business School and former director of the Centre for Health Systems and Technology.

title: University of Otago Division of Humanities Doctoral Scholarship
summary: Doctoral scholarships offered through Otago's Division of Humanities support PhD research in fields such as law, politics, history, and social inquiry, which can encompass international humanitarian law and forced migration studies. Awards typically cover tuition and a stipend.

key_figures.name: Annika Björkdahl
key_figures.title: Professor of Political Science
key_figures.research_focus: Research on peacebuilding, transitional justice, and the gendered dimensions of forced migration and humanitarian intervention.

key_figures.name: Kevin P. Clements

key_figures.research_focus: Works on peace and conflict resolution, humanitarian action, and the protection of civilians in armed conflict.

key_figures.name: Sara E. Davies
key_figures.title: Professor of International Relations
key_figures.research_focus: Examines international humanitarian law, global health governance, and the politics of forced migration and refugee protection.

title: University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship (Division of Sciences / Health Sciences research themes)
summary: Otago's central scholarship office administers doctoral funding across divisions, including research relevant to disaster management, environmental health, and global health. These awards provide fees and stipend support for meritorious PhD applicants.

key_figures.name: David McBride
key_figures.title: Associate Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Occupational and environmental health, including disaster preparedness and response, with work on emergency management and public health impacts of disasters.

key_figures.name: Philip Hill
key_figures.title: Professor

key_figures.name: Michael Baker
key_figures.title: Professor
key_figures.research_focus: Public health and epidemiology, focusing on infectious disease surveillance, pandemic preparedness, and population health policy.

title: Victoria University of Wellington Doctoral Scholarship (Humanities and Social Sciences)

key_figures.name: Jay Marlowe
key_figures.title: Professor

key_figures.name: Annemarie Munt
key_figures.title: Senior Lecturer

key_figures.name: Bethany Hine

title: Victoria University of Wellington PhD Fees Scholarship

key_figures.name: Kevin P. Clements

title: University of Auckland Doctoral Scholarship (Faculty of Medical and Health Sciences)
